item.title: México fecha portos no Pacífico enquanto furacão Polo se desloca no mar
item.description: O México fechou diversos portos do Pacífico à navegação nesta quarta-feira, enquanto o furacão Polo, uma poderosa tempestade de categoria 4, se desloca ao largo da costa sudoeste do país, levando a ameaça de chuvas fortes, inundações e condições marítimas perigosas, apesar das previsões de que ele permaneça no mar aberto.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O México fechou diversos portos do Pacífico à navegação nesta quarta-feira, enquanto o furacão Polo, uma poderosa tempestade de categoria 4, se desloca ao largo da costa sudoeste do país, levando a ameaça de chuvas fortes, inundações e condições marítimas perigosas, apesar das previsões de que ele permaneça no mar aberto. A Marinha do México informou que os portos foram fechados para todas as embarcações nos populares destinos turísticos de Acapulco e Zihuatanejo, enquanto pequenas embarcações foram impedidas de entrar em portos como Manzanillo, Lázaro Cárdenas e Puerto Escondido, à medida que as autoridades se preparam para mar agitado, ventos fortes e visibilidade reduzida. O furacão Polo ameaça a costa do Pacífico do México com chuvas fortes e ondas perigosas enquanto se desloca lentamente para noroeste, informou o Centro Nacional de Furacões dos EUA (NHC, na sigla em inglês). A expectativa é que o centro do Polo esteja próximo à costa do sudoeste do México nos próximos um ou dois dias, embora a previsão seja de que ele permaneça no mar. O NHC informou que o Estado de Guerrero poderá receber de 10 a 15 cm de chuva até quinta-feira. Os estados costeiros de Michoacán, Colima e Jalisco poderão receber de 5 a 10cm de água. As chuvas intensas devem provocar inundações e deslizamentos de terra potencialmente fatais no Estado de Guerrero, especialmente nas regiões montanhosas. Com ventos máximos sustentados próximos a 240 km/h e rajadas mais fortes, Polo continua sendo um furacão de categoria 4, depois de já ter atingido a categoria 5. “Prevê-se que haja flutuações na intensidade, mas espera-se que o Polo continue sendo um furacão muito poderoso nos próximos dias”, informou o NHC. Postos de comando estão em operação nos estados de Michoacán, Colima, Jalisco e Guerrero, informou o Ministério da Segurança mexicano em comunicado. “Eles estão coordenando inspeções de avaliação de risco, avaliações das condições, preparação de abrigos temporários e, se as condições exigirem, retiradas preventivas de pessoas”, acrescentou o ministério.

item.title: Judge appears open to blocking Trump's transgender-related limits on HIV funding
item.description: A federal judge on Wednesday appeared receptive to blocking the Trump administration from barring healthcare providers that receive certain federal HIV-treatment funds from acknowledging their transgender patients' identities or providing them gender-affirming care.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: A federal judge on Wednesday appeared receptive to blocking the Trump administration from barring healthcare providers that receive certain federal HIV-treatment funds from acknowledging their transgender patients' identities or providing them gender-affirming care. US District Judge William Young during a hearing in Boston questioned the legality of conditions imposed on the grant funding aimed at implementing an [USN:S0N3N0055 TEXT:"executive order signed"] by President Donald Trump last year prohibiting federal funding for what he calls "gender ideology." "Where does he get off issuing this?" Young asked, referring to Trump. The judge said guidelines the US Department of Health and Human Services adopted for the Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program in response to Trump's order appeared to interfere with doctor-patient relationships by preventing physicians from using a transgender patient's preferred pronouns, "even as a matter of empathy." He suggested that the policy may violate the Administrative Procedure Act by imposing an unconstitutional burden on the free speech rights of the plaintiffs, a group of national HIV medical associations and healthcare providers. Young, an appointee of Republican President Ronald Reagan, pressed a lawyer for the government on how Trump had authority to mandate such restrictions at all, saying the executive order "seems to interfere with matters that are the most private, the most sensitive to the people of the United States: their personhood." "The order of the president of the United States I think fairly read expresses the view that transgender citizens don't exist," Young told Justice Department attorney Peter Goldstone. "Please tell me I'm wrong." "I can't," Goldstone responded. The judge made his comments during a bench trial in a lawsuit that was filed in June by several HIV medical associations and providers, including the American Academy of HIV Medicine. The lawsuit centers on the Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program, which Congress created in 1990 to provide medical care for low-income and uninsured people living with HIV. Beginning in March, the Health Resources and Services Administration, a division of HHS that administers the program, added funding conditions designed to implement Trump's executive order, which had also directed the federal government to recognize only two sexes, male and female. Under the conditions, providers must ensure funding supports activities using "sex-based definitions grounded in biological reality" and not "social or medical experimentation," the lawsuit said. "It places providers with a Hobson's choice of giving up necessary funding or giving up their ability to treat their patients in an ethical manner and in a manner that is consistent with ethical standards and even state laws," said Omar Gonzalez-Pagan, a lawyer for the plaintiffs at Lambda Legal. The plaintiffs contend the policy is arbitrary and capricious under the Administrative Procedure Act because it conflicts with the Ryan White Program's statutory mandate to provide comprehensive medical services to HIV patients, which historically has included hormone therapy for transgender individuals. Goldstone urged Young to reject the case on procedural grounds, arguing that the plaintiffs lack standing as no provider has yet lost funding as a result of the restrictions. "They still have not yet had that concrete, tangible hardship because those conditions have not yet been triggered," he said. Young said he would rule "as rapidly as I can" but encouraged settlement discussions. At the parties' request, he agreed to delay a decision until after October 2 to give the administration time to consider the latest settlement proposal from the plaintiffs. The case is American Academy of HIV Medicine et al v. Health Resources and Services Administration, US District Court for the District of Massachusetts, No. 1:26-cv-12638. For the plaintiffs: Omar Gonzalez-Pagan, Jose Abrigo and Jessica Polansky of Lambda Legal For the government: Peter Goldstone of the US Department of Justice

item.title: Meta's Muse rekindles fears over winners and losers as personal AI agent emerges
item.description: Meta's Muse , the first major consumer product to emerge under Alexandr Wang since he was hired to head its AI efforts last year, has split the fortunes of US stocks this week.
item.dc:creator: Johann Cherian, Akash Sriram
item.content:encoded: Meta's Muse (META.O) , the first major [USN:L6N4500XV TEXT:"consumer product"] to emerge under Alexandr Wang since he was hired to head its AI efforts last year, has split the fortunes of US stocks this week. Muse, which allows users to delegate tasks such as shopping, travel booking and form-filling to an AI agent, overtook ChatGPT as the top free app on Apple's App Store and Google Play Store in the US and Canada. The app recorded 2.8 million downloads within two weeks of its launch, posting an average daily download growth of 55% in the first 10 days, according to market intelligence company Sensor Tower. Investors worried that Meta's scale could turn Muse into a powerful comparison-shopping tool, enabling consumers to more easily find lower-cost alternatives and weakening the loyalty that often keeps users with incumbent providers. The development dragged on several sectors this week, while Meta and AI-infrastructure related companies rallied. "Meta has really found lightning in a bottle here and someone who partners with Muse is likely to be a clear beneficiary off the bat to me. As far as net losers, it's just going to take more time to find out," said Michael O'Rourke, chief market strategist at JonesTrading. JITTERS ACROSS SECTORS Financials stocks were the hardest-hit in the previous session and remained under pressure on Wednesday on fears that the AI agent could prompt users to switch to policies with cheaper prices. Big banks such as JPMorgan (JPM.N) and Wells Fargo (WFC.N) lost more than 3% each so far this week, while brokerage Charles Schwab (SCHW.N) was down nearly 5%. Insurers such as Marsh (MRSH.N) and Arthur J. Gallagher (AJG.N) were down 2.4% and 4.6%, respectively. Art Hogan, chief market strategist for B. Riley Wealth, however, said those disruption concerns were far-fetched. "If you're going to trust the management of your finances to something that Muse found for you, then you were likely not a big payer to anyone in that industry to begin with. There's a whole lot more that goes in asset management than who's got the cheapest price," he said. Booking companies such as TripAdvisor (TRIP.O) and Booking Holdings (BKNG.O) , which rely on subscription models, have lost over 6% this week. Planet Fitness (PLNT.N) has tanked 17%, while the New York Times (NYT.N) is down 10%. Other decliners included ride-hailing companies such as Uber (UBER.N) and Lyft (LYFT.O) , and online food marketplace DoorDash (DASH.O) . THE BIGGEST WINNERS Meta's shares have soared nearly 13% this week and are set for their fifth-straight week of advances. The gains were fueled by expectations that the mainstream consumer-focused app could generate additional annual revenue, with Truist Securities estimating it to touch at least $28.5 billion by fiscal 2030. US-listed shares of Canada's Shopify have jumped 11.4% this week, after it said it would use Muse to [USN:L6N45D12F TEXT:"process checkouts"]. Payments platform PayPal (PYPL.O) has marginally gained after saying it would allow users to discover products and complete purchases through the AI agent. Privately held companies, including Stripe and Ticketmaster, also struck similar deals with Meta. MORE AI INFRASTRUCTURE DEMAND Apps such as Muse could drive AI compute demand, accelerating AI infrastructure buildout and benefiting chip stocks. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (.SOX) has gained 7% since Muse's launch and is set for its biggest two-week run since mid-August, with Nvidia (NVDA.O) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) among top gainers.

item.title: Namibia suspends livestock movement after foot-and-mouth outbreak in disease-free zone
item.description: Namibia has detected an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease in its internationally recognised disease-free zone, prompting authorities to suspend the movement, import and export of cloven-hoofed animals and their products.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Namibia has detected an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease in its internationally recognised disease-free zone, prompting authorities to suspend the movement, import and export of cloven-hoofed animals and their products. Foot-and-mouth is a highly contagious viral infection that mainly affects cattle, causing painful blisters in the mouth and on hooves. Although it is not often fatal, especially among adult cattle, it affects livestock productivity. Acting Agriculture Minister Charles Mubita told parliament on Wednesday that the disease was detected during routine surveillance on a commercial farm in the southern Kharas Region. The region borders South Africa, which is battling its worst outbreak of the disease in years and plans to vaccinate 80% of its national cattle herd of about 14 million animals. Mubita said 10 of 11 samples collected from cattle showing symptoms on September 22 tested positive the following day, confirming an active outbreak. Namibia has suspended the movement of cloven-hoofed animals and their products nationwide, and halted imports and exports of such animals until further notice, measures that Mubita said would have serious economic consequences.

item.title: Canadian dollar hits eight-week low as investors brace for domestic slowdown
item.description: The Canadian dollar weakened to an eight-week low against its US counterpart on Wednesday as the greenback notched broad-based gains and investors bet that ongoing trade uncertainty would slow Canada's economy.
item.dc:creator: Fergal Smith
item.content:encoded: The Canadian dollar weakened to an eight-week low against its US counterpart on Wednesday as the greenback notched broad-based gains and investors bet that ongoing trade uncertainty would slow Canada's economy. The loonie was trading 0.3% lower at 1.41 per US dollar, or 70.92 US cents, after touching its weakest intraday level since July 29 at 1.4106. "Markets, we think, are bracing for some softness in the economy in the coming months as US tariffs hit targeted sectors, and consumers and firms rein in spending and investment," Karl Schamotta, chief market strategist at Corpay, said in a note. "The government's tax reforms, its courting of investors and its push to sell more to the European Union should pay off over time, but the effects will be incremental and slow to arrive." New US tariffs could slash Canada's [USN:BCLLKEM29 TEXT:"fourth-quarter growth"] to below 1%, reflecting a new wave of uncertainty that threatens to hit investment and hiring, Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem said on Monday. Last week, Prime Minister Mark Carney unveiled a measure aimed at strengthening the economy, saying that Canada will let businesses immediately write off the cost of most [USN:L1N4570FS TEXT:"new capital investments"] for tax purposes. The US dollar rose to its highest level in nearly two months against a basket of major currencies as investors priced in a rate hike cycle from the Federal Reserve, while [USN:L1N45F01U TEXT:"oil prices"] jumped as comments from Iran cast doubt on progress in peace talks. US crude oil futures were trading 2.2% higher at $92.49 a barrel. Oil is one of Canada's major exports. Canadian bond yields moved higher across the curve, tracking moves in US Treasuries. The 10-year was up 11.2 basis points at 3.942%, moving back in reach of the nearly three-year high it touched last week at 3.987%. Still, it moved 1.7 basis points further below the US equivalent to a gap of about 115 basis points in favor of the US note, marking the largest gap since June 2025.

item.title: India proposes wide-ranging insurance reforms to bring down costs
item.description: India's insurance regulator proposed overhauling commission rules to cap payouts, link them to product complexity and spread life insurers' commissions beyond a policy's first year, a discussion paper released late on Wednesday showed.
item.dc:creator: Ashwin Manikandan
item.content:encoded: India's insurance regulator proposed overhauling commission rules to cap payouts, link them to product complexity and spread life insurers' commissions beyond a policy's first year, a discussion paper released late on Wednesday showed. The proposals are part of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India's push to reform the sector after New Delhi this year opened it to 100% foreign ownership, and target costs it says have ballooned since commission limits were scrapped in 2023. Reuters had [USN:L4N4340W1 TEXT:"reported"] in July that the regulator is planning reforms to curb mis-selling in the sector. Here are the key details of the proposals: The paper proposes linking commission levels to complexity of products and effort required to sell. It prescribes lower commissions for products sold via an "open architecture" such as through brokers and banks, which are large channels of sales for health, motor and life insurance. Mandatory insurance covers such as third-party motor policies would earn little or no commission. Commissions for banks and lenders selling insurance alongside loans are proposed to be capped at 2% to 5% depending on the product. Compulsory bundling of insurance with credit would be banned. Commissions on health insurance are proposed to be capped between 15% and 20% for distributors for the first time when insurance is taken. Commissions on renewal and porting of insurance to a different insurer have been capped at a lower level of 5% to 10%. Commissions on motor insurance will be capped at 5% to 10% for personal accident cover, the regulator proposed. For life insurance, the first-year commission has been capped at between 5% and 20% for distributors depending on the tenor of the policy. The regulator has sought feedback until October 25 before finalising the proposals.

item.title: Presidente do Irã acusa Trump de ter “mentalidade de intimidação” e promete não se render
item.description: O presidente iraniano, Masoud Pezeshkian, acusou o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, de ter uma “mentalidade de intimidação”, nesta quarta-feira, afirmando na ONU que o Irã não se renderá na guerra contra os EUA, mas continua aberto à diplomacia para pôr fim ao conflito.
item.dc:creator: Parisa Hafezi, Michelle Nichols
item.content:encoded: O presidente iraniano, Masoud Pezeshkian, acusou o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, de ter uma “mentalidade de intimidação”, nesta quarta-feira, afirmando na ONU que o Irã não se renderá na guerra contra os EUA, mas continua aberto à diplomacia para pôr fim ao conflito. Em um discurso em tempo de guerra perante a Assembleia Geral da ONU, composta por 193 membros, Pezeshkian disse que as ameaças apenas fortalecerão a determinação do Irã, rejeitando a advertência de Trump de que ele pode aniquilar o Irã caso não seja alcançado um acordo. “As declarações feitas ontem pelo presidente dos EUA... são um sinal de uma mentalidade de intimidação. ... O povo iraniano não se curvará à pressão. ... Aqueles que são terroristas e treinam terroristas nos chamam de terroristas”, disse ele, referindo-se à descrição feita por Trump do Irã como o principal patrocinador do terrorismo no mundo. Várias vezes durante seu discurso, Pezeshkian afirmou que o Irã está disposto a resolver as tensões com os Estados Unidos por meio de negociações, mas advertiu que Teerã não aceitaria a linguagem da força. A delegação dos Estados Unidos saiu da sala no início do discurso de Pezeshkian. A missão dos EUA junto às Nações Unidas não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário. Pezeshkian iniciou seu discurso acusando os Estados Unidos de matar civis durante a guerra, exibindo fotos que incluíam uma imagem de alunas em uma sala de aula. Um ataque com mísseis a uma escola primária em Minab, em 28 de fevereiro – horas depois que os ataques dos EUA e de Israel ao Irã deram início ao conflito – matou mais de 175 crianças e professores, segundo autoridades iranianas. O Pentágono não divulgou publicamente as conclusões de sua investigação sobre o ataque a Minab, o incidente com o maior número de vítimas civis envolvendo as Forças Armadas dos EUA em décadas. A Reuters informou em 5 de março que uma investigação interna inicial das Forças Armadas dos EUA concluiu que as forças norte-americanas provavelmente foram responsáveis pelo ataque. Pezeshkian afirmou que o Irã não tem intenção de buscar bombas nucleares, mas não abrirá mão de seu direito a um programa nuclear pacífico. “Nem armas nucleares nem abrir mão do conhecimento nuclear”, disse ele. Após sete meses de um conflito que abalou os mercados e levou o Golfo à beira de uma guerra mais ampla, Washington está lançando uma ofensiva econômica sem precedentes, depois que a ação militar não conseguiu forçar Teerã a ceder. Os líderes iranianos temem que o agravamento da situação econômica, marcado pela alta dos preços, pelo enfraquecimento do comércio e pela pressão sobre a renda das famílias, possa reacender a agitação em todo o país que tem desafiado repetidamente a República Islâmica. O Estreito de Ormuz, por onde passa um quinto do petróleo e do gás natural liquefeito do mundo, tornou-se o foco das tensões entre o Irã e os EUA. Teerã comunicou suas condições para reabrir a via navegável estratégica aos Estados Unidos por meio de mediadores, disseram fontes iranianas à Reuters. “Não pode ser que todos se beneficiem do Estreito de Ormuz enquanto nos é negado o acesso à navegação por essa via navegável. A presença permanente de frotas hostis e a expansão da guerra não levarão à paz”, disse Pezeshkian.

item.title: UNGA week could bend the war — or miss again
item.description: US President Donald Trump’s UNGA sidelines meeting with Gulf leaders this week delivered a familiar bit of Trumpian theatre: after boasting that US naval escorts had shepherded more than a billion barrels of Gulf oil, he turned to Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and quipped: “That’s not a lot to Tamim, but it’s a lot to most people.” It was classic Trump — the same long-running rich jokes he’s deployed in past Oval Office meetings and White House photo ops with Qatar’s emir, praising the state’s ability to buy “a lot of beautiful military equipment” while Tamim offers the polite, slightly nervous chuckle that has become part of their repertoire.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Mills
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump’s UNGA sidelines meeting with Gulf leaders this week delivered a familiar bit of Trumpian theatre: after boasting that US naval escorts had shepherded more than a billion barrels of Gulf oil, he turned to Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and quipped: “That’s not a lot to Tamim, but it’s a lot to most people.” It was classic Trump — the same long-running rich jokes he’s deployed in past Oval Office meetings and White House photo ops with Qatar’s emir, praising the state’s ability to buy “a lot of beautiful military equipment” while Tamim offers the polite, slightly nervous chuckle that has become part of their repertoire. The irony, of course, is sharper this year: Qatar’s economy is under its heaviest strain in decades as the US‑Israeli war on Iran and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz make it impossible to reliably export liquefied natural gas, still the country’s primary income source despite years of attempted diversification. This week’s Gulf Currents follows that diplomatic shift to New York — where Gulf leaders and foreign ministers have effectively set up camp — with reporting on Iraq’s suspension of Iranian flights under US sanctions pressure, Yemen’s accelerating displacement crisis, and Aramco’s move to carve out a standalone gas division. Our analysis asks whether UNGA can deliver a real US–Iran opening, while the chart of the week tracks the global diesel squeeze. NEWS BRIEFING Iraq [USN:S8N4320AG TEXT:"suspended Iranian flights"] to Baghdad from Wednesday after Washington threatened secondary sanctions on any airport servicing Iranian carriers. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned violators would be “knocked out of the dollar system.” Oman has similarly blocked Iranian arrivals. The move shows US sanctions pressure escalating. The UN refugee agency has warned that Houthi advances along Yemen’s Red Sea coast have [USN:L6N45E0CP TEXT:"displaced more than 130,000 people this month"], with 100,000 more projected over three months. Sea crossings to Djibouti could triple to 10,000 people as calmer weather arrives. The agency’s response plan is less than 20% funded, underscoring how the widening war’s humanitarian toll is outpacing both financial commitments and diplomatic engagement. [USN:L6N45E0RP TEXT:"Aramco plans to spin off"] a standalone gas division — its third major unit alongside upstream and downstream — with possible minority stake listings to raise cash, sources say. The move builds on Jafurah, its flagship shale gas field, and mirrors ADNOC’s playbook. It signals Aramco leaning harder into gas and outside capital as the Iran war disrupts its core oil export routes. WILL UNGA PRODUCE A TANGIBLE US–IRAN OUTCOME? It’s UNGA — the UN General Assembly’s annual gathering that packs world leaders and top diplomats into New York for a few days — and the whipsaw diplomacy in and around UN headquarters may be remembered as the moment this war’s trajectory finally turned. Or it may not. Seven months in, the fighting has only widened. The question now is whether the backroom talks happening blocks from the General Assembly floor can finally bend that curve, or whether they simply become the latest in the war’s long list of near-misses.  Even as Trump on Tuesday warned the General Assembly that he faced a choice between a deal and annihilating Iran, envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were sending messages via Qatari shuttles to Iranian officials a few blocks away. Trump called it “a very good meeting”, while Gulf leaders huddled with US officials on next steps. UNGA has produced real openings before. In 2013, then-US Secretary of State John Kerry and Iranian Foreign Minister Javad Zarif held the first US-Iran foreign minister contact since 1979 — a tentative sidelines meeting that, almost two years later, became the JCPOA nuclear deal that curbed Iran’s enrichment program in exchange for sanctions relief.  Last year, a meeting on the UNGA sidelines anchored by Trump and Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan, brought Arab and Muslim leaders together on Gaza and produced a joint declaration underpinning what became the US-brokered ceasefire and hostage-release framework. It represented a more recent template for how the Trump administration has built multilateral cover for a deal.  What makes UNGA week structurally different from ordinary diplomacy is proximity: nearly every relevant player is in Manhattan simultaneously, collapsing weeks of protocol into hallway conversations. This year, the proximity isn’t starting cold, since Iran had already conveyed its response to a new proposal to mediators before the week began, and Qatar has been circulating draft language between the two sides. Having Trump, Witkoff, Kushner, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi and the Gulf states all in the same city at once is the precondition for a breakthrough, however — not a guarantee of one. A few clear tests will tell us whether this week produced real movement: Iran has signalled it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within days if Washington eases its blockade and unfreezes assets, which would be a specific, verifiable marker. Will Qatar’s draft surface publicly? Will Araqchi meet US officials again before Iran’s delegation leaves Saturday? And will Saudi Arabia — most exposed by September’s advance by Yemen’s Houthis, yet still absent from the visible diplomatic track — get pulled in? No matter what gets negotiated in Midtown Manhattan this week, what happens on the ground back in the Gulf has the potential to spoil it all. This war is being fought across multiple active fronts at once — Houthi missiles over the Red Sea, tankers threading the Strait of Hormuz, pipelines and export terminals within easy reach of Iranian-aligned groups — and a single incident on any of them could eclipse the entire diplomatic process. CHART OF THE WEEK The global diesel shortage driven by wars in Iran and Ukraine is unlikely to ease before next year, according to storage market indicators and industry participants, extending a spike in fuel costs that is weighing on economies worldwide. [USN:L6N450107 TEXT:"Shariq Khan and Siddharth Cavale examine diesel prices, stockpiles, and availability of storage facility leases"] for insights on market expectations. LAST WAVE: Houthis seize strategic highlands as Riyadh comes under fire Houthi fighters [USN:L1N45D0B1 TEXT:"pushed into Yemen’s highlands"] this week, seizing strategic ground meant to sever the Red Sea coast from Saudi-backed government territory — a lightning advance that has already displaced nearly 130,000 people and, according to the UN, killed close to 700. Riyadh was apparently struck for the first time since the war widened, with explosions heard and a column of black smoke rising from near the airport, and Trump reportedly called off retaliatory US strikes at the last minute as bombs were being loaded onto aircraft. Yemeni analyst Mohammed Al-Qadhi called the fighting for the Kahboub Mountains potentially decisive: “These mountains could become critical to determining whether the Houthis succeed in consolidating their recent territorial gains.” Saudi Arabia has meanwhile rerouted oil exports through Hormuz at record wartime fees, with Britain and France stepping in militarily to provide Saudi Arabia with refuelling and infrastructure protection.

item.title: EUA estão abertos a prorrogar trégua comercial com a China ou a fechar acordo maior, diz Bessent
item.description: Os Estados Unidos estão abertos a prorrogar a trégua comercial entre com a China, que expira em 10 de novembro, ou a considerar um acordo comercial possivelmente maior, afirmou o secretário do Tesouro norte-americano, Scott Bessent, nesta quarta-feira, ao sair de uma reunião com o vice-primeiro-ministro chinês He Lifeng para preparar uma cúpula entre os líderes dos dois países.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal
item.content:encoded: Os Estados Unidos estão abertos a prorrogar a trégua comercial entre com a China, que expira em 10 de novembro, ou a considerar um acordo comercial possivelmente maior, afirmou o secretário do Tesouro norte-americano, Scott Bessent, nesta quarta-feira, ao sair de uma reunião com o vice-primeiro-ministro chinês He Lifeng para preparar uma cúpula entre os líderes dos dois países. Bessent não deu detalhes sobre um possível acordo comercial mais abrangente entre os EUA e a China após sua segunda reunião com He em quatro dias. Os presidentes dos EUA, Donald Trump, e da China, Xi Jinping, devem discutir as questões mais a fundo na Casa Branca na quinta-feira. “No domingo, os chineses sugeriram a ideia de um acordo maior e, considerando que este pode ser um ano histórico em que os líderes se encontrem até quatro vezes — sendo esta a segunda reunião, em Shenzhen e depois em Miami —, estamos abertos à ideia de simplesmente dar continuidade ao acordo de Busan ou de analisar o acordo maior”, disse Bessent a repórteres. “Estamos de acordo com ambas as opções e faremos o que for melhor para o povo norte-americano.” Bessent havia descrito anteriormente a reunião na sede do Banco Mundial, em Washington, como uma forma de esclarecer algumas “questões pendentes” antes da cúpula entre Trump e Xi, e afirmou que o governo Trump busca estabilidade estratégica baseada em “reciprocidade e justiça”. Mas suas declarações após a reunião foram o sinal mais forte até agora de que uma prorrogação da trégua comercial firmada no ano passado em Busan, na Coreia do Sul, está na pauta da cúpula entre Trump e Xi. Bessent, He e o representante comercial dos EUA, Jamieson Greer, se reuniram em Nova York no domingo, em um esforço para preparar possíveis acordos comerciais e de inteligência artificial para que os dois líderes os analisassem. Bessent caracterizou essas negociações como “bem-sucedidas”, afirmando que os dois lados concordaram em lançar uma “linha direta” de comunicação para notificar um ao outro sobre incidentes de segurança relacionados à IA. A resposta da China ao plano da linha direta de IA não ficou clara, com a agência de notícias estatal Xinhua reconhecendo apenas que as duas partes discutiram o tema. (Reportagem de Andrea Shalal e David Lawder; reportagem adicional de Susan Heavey)

item.title: India cuts import duty on palm oil, soyoil and sunflower oil
item.description: India has cut the basic import duty on crude and refined edible oils, including palm oil, soyoil and sunflower oil, the government said in a notification late on Wednesday, as it seeks to lower prices during the peak festive season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India has cut the basic import duty on crude and refined edible oils, including palm oil, soyoil and sunflower oil, the government said in a notification late on Wednesday, as it seeks to lower prices during the peak festive season. The basic import duty on crude palm oil and crude soyoil has been reduced to 5% from 10%, the notification said.

item.title: Reports: Giants' Jaxson Dart expected to have season-ending surgery
item.description: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is expected to undergo surgery to repair multiple injuries to his left knee and will miss the remainder of the 2026 season, NFL Network reported Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is expected to undergo surgery to repair multiple injuries to his left knee and will miss the remainder of the 2026 season, NFL Network reported Wednesday. Dart took a blow to the knee on his team's opening drive during Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. The 23-year-old missed the remainder of the game. Initial tests Monday night created optimism that Dart avoided a major knee injury. Giants head coach John Harbaugh said after the game that the injury was "in the neighborhood" of a sprained medial collateral ligament. An MRI on Tuesday, though, ultimately revealed that while Dart's ACL is intact, he has meniscus, MCL and PCL damage, with the meniscus being the most concerning of the three. According to the report, knee surgery focused on the meniscus and MCL gives Dart the best chance at a full recovery heading toward the 2027 season. Dart was replaced in Monday's game by Jameis Winston, who completed 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards. He also threw an interception. Dart was the 25th overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. He's currently 31st in the NFL with 250 passing yards and tied for 14th with three TD passes, all in New York's Week 1 win over the Dallas Cowboys. New York could contemplate acquiring a quarterback. Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy has worked closely with current NFL backups Mitchell Trubisky (Tennessee Titans) and Justin Fields (Kansas City Chiefs) when he was head coach of the Chicago Bears. "Absolute faith in all our players," Harbaugh said about Winston. "That's why all the guys are here. Jameis is one of our guys who obviously is here for a reason. He's a very good football player." The Giants (1-1) host the Titans (0-2) on Sunday. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bolsas europeas caen ante falta de avances en negociaciones EEUU-Irán
item.description: Las bolsas europeas cerraron a la baja el miércoles, mientras los precios del petróleo repuntaban hasta superar los 100 dólares por barril, lo que volvió a impulsar al alza los rendimientos de los bonos públicos, en un contexto en el que el conflicto con Irán no daba señales de llegar a su fin.
item.dc:creator: Sudeshna Ghoshal, Purvi Agarwal
item.content:encoded: Las bolsas europeas cerraron a la baja el miércoles, mientras los precios del petróleo repuntaban hasta superar los 100 dólares por barril, lo que volvió a impulsar al alza los rendimientos de los bonos públicos, en un contexto en el que el conflicto con Irán no daba señales de llegar a su fin. * El índice de referencia paneuropeo STOXX 600 (.STOXX) perdió un 0,4%, revirtiendo las ganancias registradas a primera hora de la sesión. La mayoría de las principales bolsas regionales también cedieron terreno. * Los futuros del crudo Brent subían más de un 1%, superando el nivel clave de los 100 dólares por barril. De todas formas, se mantenían en sus niveles más bajos en dos semanas, alcanzados tras cinco sesiones de caídas. * Los mercados analizaron los discursos enfrentados de Irán y Estados Unidos en la Asamblea General de la ONU. El presidente iraní, Masud Pezeshkian, dijo que Teherán nunca se rendiría, un día después de que el presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, utilizó el mismo foro para amenazar con "aniquilar" a Irán. * El rendimiento del bono alemán a 10 años , referencia para la zona del euro, se situaba en el 3,550%, mientras que el retorno de la deuda de los bonos del Tesoro estadounidense a 10 años subía hasta el 5,085%, su nivel más alto desde 2007. * "Es evidente que había cierta esperanza de que se entablara un diálogo que pudiera acelerar el fin del conflicto, pero no parece que se haya avanzado mucho", dijo Steve Sosnick, analista jefe de mercados de Interactive Brokers. "Hemos avanzado mucho en poco tiempo, por lo que hoy estábamos preparados para una ligera toma de ganancias". * La mayoría de los principales sectores del STOXX 600 registraron caídas, excepto los valores energéticos (.SXEP) , que ganaron un 1,3%. * Las acciones de los grandes bancos (.SX7P) perdieron un 0,4%, mientras que los sectores de seguros (.SXIP) y de construcción y materiales (.SXOP) registraron las mayores caídas porcentuales, con descensos del 1,7% y el 1,3%, respectivamente. * Estos movimientos se producen tras el fuerte repunte de los mercados globales esta semana. El STOXX 600 sigue registrando una subida del 0,8% esta semana, tras haber registrado caídas durante las últimas tres semanas, gracias al repunte de los precios del petróleo y de los rendimientos de los bonos, y a que el Banco Central Europeo aplicó su segunda subida de tasas de interés este año.

item.title: Les Pays-Bas mettent fin à leur boycott de l'Eurovision et y participeront en 2027
item.description: Les Pays-Bas feront leur retour au Concours Eurovision de la chanson en 2027, mettant fin à leur boycott lié à la participation d’Israël, la chaîne publique NPO prenant en charge la candidature néerlandaise.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les Pays-Bas feront leur retour au Concours Eurovision de la chanson en 2027, mettant fin à leur boycott lié à la participation d’Israël, la chaîne publique NPO prenant en charge la candidature néerlandaise. Les Pays-Bas avaient boudé le concours en 2026 pour protester contre la présence d’Israël. Le mois dernier, AvroTros, le diffuseur qui s’occupait jusqu'à présent de la candidature néerlandaise, a déclaré qu’il boycotterait à nouveau l’événement en 2027. Mais AvroTros avait laissé la décision finale concernant la participation néerlandaise entre les mains d’autres chaînes aux Pays-Bas, passant ainsi le relais à la chaîne NPO. Cette dernière a déclaré mercredi que l’Union européenne de radio-télévision avait pris des "mesures importantes" en réponse aux critiques formulées par les pays qui n’avaient pas participé en 2026, ce qui, selon elle, devrait conduire à un événement plus "fédérateur". La NPO a toutefois reconnu que cette décision susciterait des "sentiments mitigés" dans le pays. L[USN:L6N4590Q0 TEXT:"'Irlande a annoncé"] qu'elle ne participerait pas au concours de 2027, pour la deuxième année consécutive, invoquant les pertes humaines persistantes à Gaza. Lors de l'édition 2026, l’Irlande, les Pays-Bas, l’Islande, l’Espagne et la Slovénie avaient boycotté le Concours Eurovision de la chanson pour protester contre la participation d’Israël et son offensive militaire dans l'enclave palestinienne. Un cessez-le-feu dans la guerre de Gaza est entré en vigueur en octobre 2025, mais n’a pas complètement mis fin aux attaques israéliennes. La guerre a été déclenchée par l’attaque menée par le Hamas contre Israël le 7 octobre 2023, faisant quelque 1.200 victimes. Selon les autorités palestiniennes, plus de 73.000 personnes ont été tuées lors de l'offensive israélienne contre la bande de Gaza.

item.title: Colts place WR Alec Pierce (heel) on injured reserve
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts are placing wide receiver Alec Pierce on injured reserve with a left heel injury, head coach Shane Steichen confirmed Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Indianapolis Colts are placing wide receiver Alec Pierce on injured reserve with a left heel injury, head coach Shane Steichen confirmed Wednesday. Pierce will miss a minimum of four games after aggravating the injury during Sunday night's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. He is not eligible to return until the Week 7 game at Minnesota on Oct. 25. Multiple outlets have reported that the Colts hope to avoid another surgery on the same foot that was surgically repaired in March. Streichen defended the team's management of Pierce's injury. "We went through that rebab process, he hit all his landmarks, hit all his benchmarks, and then obviously we eased him back into practice," Steichen said. "The trainers and doctors felt good about it, (Pierce) felt good about it to go play, we limited him in practice working those first two weeks, he had limited reps Week 1. "Injuries happen. You never want to see it happen, but we would have never put him on the field if we didn't feel good about it and he didn't feel good about it." Signed to a four-year, $114 million contract extension on March 9, Pierce had one reception for 11 yards on Sunday. He caught four passes for 61 yards in the Week 1 loss to the Baltimore Ravens. Pierce, 26, led the NFL in yards per reception in each of the past two seasons. He averaged 22.3 yards in 2024 and 21.3 last season when he had the first 1,000-yard season of his career. A second-round pick by Indianapolis in 2022, Pierce has 162 receptions for 3,006 yards and 17 touchdowns through 66 career games (56 starts). The Colts (0-2) signed veteran wide receiver Darius Slayton to the practice squad on Tuesday. He played with Colts quarterback Daniel Jones with the New York Giants from 2019-24 and could potentially be activated for Sunday's game against the visiting Houston Texans (0-2). Indianapolis also signed wide receiver Eli Pancol to the practice squad on Wednesday. He participated in training camp with the Colts before being released in final roster cuts. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ações recuam com alta do petróleo e rendimentos por falta de avanço em paz entre EUA e Irã
item.description: As ações europeias fecharam em baixa nesta quarta-feira com os preços do petróleo avançando para mais de US$100 por barril, o que voltou a elevar os rendimentos dos títulos públicos uma vez que o conflito no Irã não mostra sinais de acabar.
item.dc:creator: Sudeshna Ghoshal, Purvi Agarwal
item.content:encoded: As ações europeias fecharam em baixa nesta quarta-feira com os preços do petróleo avançando para mais de US$100 por barril, o que voltou a elevar os rendimentos dos títulos públicos uma vez que o conflito no Irã não mostra sinais de acabar. O índice de referência pan-europeu STOXX 600 (.STOXX) encerrou com queda de 0,4%, revertendo os ganhos registrados mais cedo na sessão. Os futuros do petróleo Brent subiram mais de 1%, ultrapassando a marca crucial de US$100 por barril. Eles se mantiveram nos níveis mais baixos em duas semanas, atingidos após cinco pregões de quedas. Os mercados analisaram discursos contraditórios do Irã e dos EUA na Assembleia Geral da ONU. O presidente iraniano, Masoud Pezeshkian, afirmou que Teerã nunca se renderá aos EUA, um dia depois de o presidente norte-americano, Donald Trump, ter usado o mesmo fórum para ameaçar “aniquilar” o Irã. O rendimento do título alemão de 10 anos , referência para a zona do euro, estava em 3,550%, enquanto o rendimento do Treasury de 10 anos subiu para 5,085%, o maior nível desde 2007. “Havia claramente alguma esperança de que houvesse um diálogo capaz de acelerar o fim do conflito, mas não parece que tenha havido muito progresso”, disse Steve Sosnick, analista-chefe de mercado da Interactive Brokers. “Avançamos bastante em um curto período de tempo, então estávamos preparados para uma pequena realização de lucros hoje.” A maioria dos principais setores do STOXX 600 registrou queda, com exceção das ações de energia (.SXEP) , que subiram 1,3%. As ações dos grandes bancos (.SX7P) caíram 0,4%, enquanto os setores de seguros (.SXIP) e de construção e materiais (.SXOP) registraram as maiores quedas em termos percentuais, com recuos de 1,7% e 1,3%, respectivamente. Em LONDRES, o índice Financial Times (.FTSE) recuou 0,03%, a 10.705,26 pontos. Em FRANKFURT, o índice DAX (.GDAXI) caiu 0,66%, a 25.410,63 pontos. Em PARIS, o índice CAC-40 (.FCHI) perdeu 0,39%, a 8.123,41 pontos. Em MILÃO, o índice Ftse/Mib (.FTMIB) teve desvalorização de 0,21%, a 51.987,49 pontos. Em MADRI, o índice Ibex-35 (.IBEX) registrou baixa de 0,62%, a 19.632,20 pontos. Em LISBOA, o índice PSI20 (.PSI20) desvalorizou-se 0,25%, a 9.632,44 pontos.

item.title: Microsoft planeja investimento de mais de US$10 bi no Oriente Médio
item.description: A Microsoft planeja investir mais de US$10 bilhões nos Emirados Árabes Unidos, na Arábia Saudita, no Catar e no Kuwait até 2030, inclusive em infraestrutura de computação em nuvem e inteligência artificial, afirmou um executivo sênior nesta quarta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Federico Maccioni
item.content:encoded: A Microsoft (MSFT.O) planeja investir mais de US$10 bilhões nos Emirados Árabes Unidos, na Arábia Saudita, no Catar e no Kuwait até 2030, inclusive em infraestrutura de computação em nuvem e inteligência artificial, afirmou um executivo sênior nesta quarta-feira. A gigante tecnológica norte-americana está tornando a resiliência digital uma parte fundamental de sua estratégia para a região, à medida que a guerra com o Irã continua. O investimento da Microsoft reflete tanto sua “construção contínua de infraestrutura quanto a expansão das operações na região”, disse o vice-presidente e presidente, Brad Smith, à Reuters. Os países do Golfo estão injetando bilhões em IA enquanto se esforçam para se tornarem centros globais que ajudem a diversificar suas economias para além do petróleo e do gás, apostando que a abundância de terras e o acesso a energia barata atrairão grandes empresas de tecnologia, incluindo a Microsoft. No entanto, ainda há desafios em áreas como o acesso a chips avançados e a incerteza trazida pela guerra, incluindo ataques a centrais de processamento de dados, como as instalações da AWS, a unidade de computação em nuvem da Amazon (AMZN.O) , no Barein e nos Emirados Árabes Unidos. “Estamos mantendo todos os investimentos que planejávamos fazer antes do início deste conflito e, na verdade, estamos ampliando-os... É um plano de gastos agressivo”, disse Smith. O executivo disse que a Microsoft apoiou parceiros locais durante o conflito, inclusive com avaliações de resiliência digital, já na primeira semana do conflito, que teve início em 28 de fevereiro. RESILIÊNCIA DIGITAL A Microsoft está agora trabalhando para ajudar os países do Golfo em áreas como preparação e proteção de dados críticos, como parte de uma iniciativa de resiliência digital. A empresa não pôde fornecer um detalhamento do investimento planejado por país ou projeto específico, disse Smith, citando fatores que incluem a segurança. Embora os Emirados Árabes Unidos tenham sido amplamente poupados de ataques desde maio, vários outros países do Golfo continuam enfrentando ameaças. A Microsoft também planeja investir mais de US$400 milhões em conectividade submarina e terrestre em todo o Oriente Médio até 2030. Além disso, está fortalecendo sua parceria com empresas nacionais de IA, incluindo a G42, de Abu Dhabi, na qual a Microsoft investiu US$1,5 bilhão para adquirir uma participação minoritária em 2024, garantindo à empresa norte-americana um assento no conselho de administração, atualmente ocupado por Smith. A Microsoft está trabalhando com a Humain, da Arábia Saudita, e a Qai, do Catar, “em áreas específicas que são prioritárias para elas”, disse ele, ressaltando que não planeja fazer investimentos de capital nessas empresas.

item.title: Irán comunicó a EEUU las condiciones para reanudar relaciones diplomáticas, según ministerio de Exteriores
item.description: Irán comunicó a Estados Unidos sus condiciones para reactivar las relaciones diplomáticas, en un intercambio de mensajes de dos horas de duración a través de un mediador al margen de la Asamblea General de la ONU el martes, dijo el miércoles en X el portavoz del ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Irán, Esmaeil Baghaei.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Irán comunicó a Estados Unidos sus condiciones para reactivar las relaciones diplomáticas, en un intercambio de mensajes de dos horas de duración a través de un mediador al margen de la Asamblea General de la ONU el martes, dijo el miércoles en X el portavoz del ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Irán, Esmaeil Baghaei. Las condiciones transmitidas a través de un mediador qatarí incluían la aceptación de la ruta segura en el estrecho de Ormuz —sobre la que se ha alcanzado un acuerdo entre los dos países ribereños—, el cese de las medidas estadounidenses contra Irán, incluido el "terrorismo" económico y el bloqueo naval, la liberación de los activos congelados y el fin de la guerra en todos los frentes, afirmó.

item.title: Shorter races a good compromise, says F1 champion Norris
item.description: McLaren’s reigning world champion Lando Norris on Wednesday described Formula One’s move to shorten races next year as a good, short-term compromise that would improve the racing action.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Takle
item.content:encoded: McLaren’s reigning world champion Lando Norris on Wednesday described Formula One’s move to shorten races next year as a good, short-term compromise that would improve the racing action. The governing FIA's Formula One commission on Monday agreed to reduce the standard Grand Prix distance from 305 km to 290 km from 2027, cutting races by two or three laps. The move is aimed at ensuring drivers make it to the end of races without running out of fuel, with the fuel flow rate set to increase next year. “It's a good compromise that we need to make to make our sport better and rely more on driving rather than who can look after our battery the best,” Briton Norris told reporters. “I think in a few years' time when all engine manufacturers are on board with having more fuel again and having bigger tanks and all of that, then it's something we can go back to, the longer races and the races that we've always had in Formula One,” added the 26-year-old. The fuel flow rate permitted by the rules will increase by 5% next season, as part of a rebalancing of the split between combustion engine and electric power to 58-42 from the current 53-47. It will increase again by 13% in 2028, with the combustion engine-electric power split rising to 60-40. The move is aimed at allowing for more flat-out driving and less energy management after widespread complaints about the racing having become more artificial. Red Bull’s four-times champion Max Verstappen, a vocal critic of the sport’s current hybrid rules, said shortening the race distance would be worth it if it made the racing better. “I mean I would run 50% less if it would give me a nicer engine to drive,” joked the Dutchman. “But, I don’t think it’s a big problem. If we have to shorten it a little bit for the fuel consumption but for overall a better racing experience then I think everyone will take it.” Ferrari rival and seven-times world champion Lewis Hamilton, however, opposed the move. “This is supposed to be the sport which is the most physically and mentally demanding and there are some (races) that are so hot and you are on the edge,” said the 41-year-old. “But that is where you want to see athletes, right on the edge of performance…”

item.title: Microsoft plans $10 billion-plus Gulf investment with focus on resilience
item.description: Microsoft is planning to invest more than $10 billion across the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Kuwait between now and 2030, including in cloud and AI infrastructure, a senior executive said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Federico Maccioni
item.content:encoded: Microsoft (MSFT.O) is planning to invest more than $10 billion across the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Kuwait between now and 2030, including in cloud and AI infrastructure, a senior executive said on Wednesday. The US tech giant is making digital resilience a key part of its strategy for the region as the Iran war rumbles on . Microsoft's investment reflects both its "ongoing build-out of infrastructure and also the expansion of operations in the region," Vice Chair and President Brad Smith told Reuters. Gulf countries are pouring billions into AI as they strive to become global hubs to help diversify their economies away from oil and gas, betting that land abundance and access to cheap energy will lure hyperscalers, including Microsoft. However, challenges remain in areas including access to advanced chips and the uncertainty brought by the war, including [USN:L6N4570O0 TEXT:"attacks"] on data centres such as Amazon (AMZN.O) cloud unit AWS's facilities in Bahrain and the UAE. "We're sustaining all the investments we planned to make before this conflict started, and we're in fact adding to them ... It's an aggressive spending schedule," said Smith. He said Microsoft had supported local partners during the conflict, including with digital resilience assessments, even in the first week of the conflict, which began on February 28. DIGITAL RESILIENCE Microsoft is now working to help the Gulf countries in areas such as readiness and critical data protection as part of a digital resilience initiative. It could not provide a breakdown of the planned investment by country or specific project, Smith said, citing factors including security. While the UAE has been largely spared attacks since May, several other Gulf countries have continued to face threats. Microsoft also plans to invest more than $400 million in subsea and terrestrial connectivity across the Middle East by 2030. It is also strengthening its partnership with national AI companies, including Abu Dhabi's G42, in which Microsoft invested $1.5 billion for a minority stake in 2024, giving the US firm a board seat currently filled by Smith. Microsoft is working with Saudi Arabia's Humain and Qatar's Qai "in selected areas that are priorities for them," he said, noting that it does not plan capital investments in the firms.

item.title: Lavrov e Rubio discutem relações bilaterais e agenda internacional, diz Rússia
item.description: O ministro das Relações Exteriores da Rússia, Sergei Lavrov, e o secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, discutiram uma ampla gama de questões da agenda bilateral e internacional em uma reunião realizada na quarta-feira, informou o Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Rússia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O ministro das Relações Exteriores da Rússia, Sergei Lavrov, e o secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, discutiram uma ampla gama de questões da agenda bilateral e internacional em uma reunião realizada na quarta-feira, informou o Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Rússia. Lavrov e Rubio discutiram a situação em várias regiões, incluindo a Ucrânia e o Oriente Médio. O ministério informou que Lavrov enfatizou a necessidade de restabelecer as relações bilaterais o mais rápido possível, enquanto as duas partes concordaram em dar continuidade às discussões.

item.title: Mps, AD: voto 29 ottobre preserva opzioni su offerte
item.description: Gli azionisti di Monte dei Paschi dovrebbero considerare il voto del 29 ottobre sulla strategia difensiva della banca contro l'offerta di acquisizione di Intesa Sanpaolo come uno strumento per preservare le diverse opzioni, secondo l'AD Luigi Lovaglio.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Gli azionisti di Monte dei Paschi (BMPS.MI) dovrebbero considerare il voto del 29 ottobre sulla strategia difensiva della banca contro l'offerta di acquisizione di Intesa Sanpaolo (ISP.MI) come uno strumento per preservare le diverse opzioni, secondo l'AD Luigi Lovaglio. Intervenendo a una conferenza di Bank of America a Londra, Lovaglio ha detto che il voto non dovrebbe essere interpretato come una scelta tra l'offerta di Intesa e l'operazione alternativa proposta da Mps.

item.title: Report: Trump expected to make Presidents Cup appearance
item.description: President Donald J. Trump is expected to attend Sunday's final round of the Presidents Cup golf competition at Medinah Country Club near Chicago, Front Office Sports reported Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: President Donald J. Trump is expected to attend Sunday's final round of the Presidents Cup golf competition at Medinah Country Club near Chicago, Front Office Sports reported Wednesday. The biennial event gets underway on Thursday with the U.S. squad looking for its 11th straight victory against the International (non-European) Team. Trump previously accepted an invitation from the PGA Tour to serve as an honorary chairman of the event. "I look forward to being there," Trump said in an announcement last month. He did not specify which date(s) he would attend, and the PGA Tour declined to comment on the president's travel plans for security reasons. The White House did not respond to a request for comment from FOS. During his first term in office, Trump attended the 2017 Presidents Cup at Liberty National Golf Club in New Jersey. He became the first sitting U.S. president to present the trophy to the winning team following the Americans' 19-11 victory. Last year, Trump became the first sitting U.S. president to attend the Ryder Cup. He was on site for the opening day of the competition at Bethpage Black Golf Course in New York. The Presidents Cup will be the fifth high-profile golf event attended this year by Trump, but the first at a golf course he does not own. He was at LIV Golf events at his clubs in Virginia and New Jersey, the PGA Tour tournament at Doral and the Irish Open in Doonbeg. --Field Level Media

item.title: EU and Canada secure €211 million for ocean observation activities
item.description: The European Commission and Canada have secured at least €211 million ($240 million) in funding pledges for a newly launched ocean observation initiative, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Wednesday at the UN General Assembly in New York.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The European Commission and Canada have secured at least €211 million ($240 million) in funding pledges for a newly launched ocean observation initiative, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Wednesday at the UN General Assembly in New York. The OceanEye International Alliance for the Global Ocean Observing System, which so far comprises 30 country members and the European Union, aims to support safe navigation, weather forecasting, climate prediction, coastal protection and the naval economy. "We must listen to the ocean and we must protect it much more. And yet, ocean observation is under huge pressure. The global network that provides this data faces a critical funding shortfall," von der Leyen said. She said the EU had increased its funding for ocean observation activities with a seed round of €92 million, while Canada's Carney said that his country would spend 82 million Canadian dollars ($58 million) over five years for this purpose. The funding will support the observing networks by developing technologies, as well as adding more equipment in the high seas and in space such as sensors and satellites. ($1 = 0.8780 euros) ($1 = 1.4100 Canadian dollars)
