item.description: [２３日 ロイター] - 米シカゴ地区連銀のグールズビー総裁は２３日、連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）は、現在のエネルギーシ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米シカゴ連銀総裁、原油ショックに警戒　持続的なインフレ要因の恐れ 1:29 配信

米シカゴ地区連銀のグールズビー総裁。カリフォルニア州ビバリーヒルズで５月撮影。REUTERS/Mike Blake

[２３日　ロイター] - 米シカゴ地区連銀のグールズビー総裁は２３日、連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）は、現在のエネルギーショックが自然と解消されると期待するのではなく、インフレを持続的に押し上げる要因として扱う必要があるとの認識を示した。

グールズビー氏は２３日公開のポッドキャスト番組「エコノミクス・アプライド」で、「大きな負の供給ショックについては、最初からインフレへの影響がかなり持続すると想定しておいたほうがいい」と指摘。コロナ禍や関税措置発動時にも同じことが起き、原油ショックについても同じことが起きている可能性があるため「われわれは注意すべきだ」と述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：米景気拡大維持、ＦＲＢの利下げペース次第 アングル：米長期金利5％接近で株式市場に警戒感、決算後はマクロ要因に注目 焦点：ベセント氏発言で強まる日銀9月利上げ観測、米国の影響力拡大に懸念も アングル：米国債「ツイスト・スティープ化」、ＦＲＢの信認巡る懸念反映か アングル：インフレで揺らぐ債券のヘッジ機能、米投資家は実物資産に移行 最終更新: 9/24(木) 1:29 ロイター

item.title: Goolsbee, de la Fed, dice que "más vale que seamos cautelosos" ante avance del petróleo
item.description: El presidente de la Reserva Federal de Chicago, Austan Goolsbee, cree que el banco central estadounidense podría tener que considerar el actual choque de la energía como una fuente de inflación persistente, en lugar de esperar que se disipe por sí sola.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de la Reserva Federal de Chicago, Austan Goolsbee, cree que el banco central estadounidense podría tener que considerar el actual choque de la energía como una fuente de inflación persistente, en lugar de esperar que se disipe por sí sola. "En el caso de grandes perturbaciones negativas en la oferta... es mejor partir de la base desde el principio de que esto va a tener un efecto bastante persistente sobre la inflación: sin duda, eso es lo que ocurrió con el COVID-19; eso es lo que ocurrió con los aranceles. Y quizá sea lo que está ocurriendo con el petróleo", dijo Goolsbee en el podcast "Economics, Applied", publicado el miércoles. "Así que más vale que seamos cautelosos".

item.title: Crew 2 coach axed after telling female ref it's a 'man's game'
item.description: The Columbus Crew have fired Crew 2 head coach Federico Higuain over a sexist confrontation with a female referee last month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Columbus Crew have fired Crew 2 head coach Federico Higuain over a sexist confrontation with a female referee last month. Higuain, a star forward for the Crew from 2012-19, has coached the franchise's MLS NEXT Pro affiliate since Jan. 29, 2025. During an Aug. 23 match against Huntsville City FC, Higuain "strongly" shook the hand of a female official and told her, "Don't forget, this is a man's game," according to The Athletic. Higuain, 41, received a red card and served a two-match suspension after the mid-game incident. He returned to the team earlier this month and coached in three additional games. On Sunday, the referees' union released a statement calling the two-match ban insufficient for "two deliberate acts of physical abuse and sexism." The Crew parted ways with Higuain on Tuesday. "We determined it's in the best interest of our Club, players and support staff to dismiss Federico Higuain from his responsibilities," general manager Issa Tall said in a statement. "After conversations this week and further assessing the past month, our Club's standards of what's expected from a leader for one of our teams have not been met." Higuain tallied 60 goals and 67 assists in 232 career MLS matches with Columbus, D.C. United (2020) and Inter Miami (2020-21). The Argentina native was the MLS Newcomer of the Year in 2012. --Field Level Media

item.title: Nucleare, ok definitivo al Senato. Meloni: "Scelta di buon senso"
item.description: Oggi il Senato ha approvato in via definitiva una legge volta a rilanciare la produzione di energia nucleare, a quasi 40 anni dal referendum che aveva portato alla chiusura dei reattori in Italia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Oggi il Senato ha approvato in via definitiva una legge volta a rilanciare la produzione di energia nucleare, a quasi 40 anni dal referendum che aveva portato alla chiusura dei reattori in Italia. Il governo punta a utilizzare reattori modulari avanzati per contribuire alla decarbonizzazione dell’industria e rafforzare la sicurezza energetica, sostenendo che i progressi tecnologici e in materia di sicurezza abbiano reso obsoleto il voto antinucleare del 1987. La premier Giorgia Meloni su X ha parlato di "una scelta coraggiosa e di buon senso", spiegando che questa svolta comporta maggiore sicurezza energetica con una minore dipendenza dall'estero e una minore esposizione alle crisi internazionali, e rappresenta "una risposta concreta alla domanda di elettricità che crescerà con data center e intelligenza artificiale". Il governo sta cercando di proteggere l'economia dall'impennata dei prezzi dell'energia innescata dai conflitti in Medio Oriente, rilanciando gli appelli a ridurre la dipendenza dalle forniture energetiche estere. "Il nucleare sostenibile, insieme alle rinnovabili, renderà l'Italia un Paese sicuro, indipendente e competitivo", ha detto il ministro dell’Energia Gilberto Pichetto Fratin dopo la votazione. L’Italia dipende fortemente dalle importazioni energetiche, compresa l’elettricità generata dalle centrali nucleari di Paesi confinanti come la Francia, ma gli attivisti antinucleari sostengono che i timori in materia di sicurezza e le lunghe tempistiche necessarie per la costruzione di nuovi reattori superino qualsiasi beneficio derivante dal rilancio del settore. Gli italiani restano divisi sulla questione. Secondo un sondaggio condotto a giugno da Demopolis, il 51% era favorevole al rilancio della produzione di energia nucleare, ma la maggioranza si opponeva alla costruzione di una centrale vicino alla propria abitazione. Al momento della presentazione del piano lo scorso anno, il governo aveva stimato che se l'energia nucleare arrivasse a rappresentare almeno l'11% del mix energetico italiano si potrebbero risparmiare 17 miliardi di euro in costi di decarbonizzazione entro il 2050. Il piano nazionale per l’energia e il clima prevede che tale quota possa arrivare al 22%. La legge concede al governo 12 mesi per adottare i decreti attuativi necessari al rilancio della produzione di energia nucleare e prevede accantonamenti per la dismissione dei vecchi impianti e l’istituzione di un’autorità di regolamentazione indipendente. I partiti dell’opposizione di centro-sinistra si sono in gran parte opposti alla misura e hanno esortato il governo a non destinare ulteriori terreni alla costruzione di nuovi reattori. "Eventuali nuovi impianti siano localizzati prioritariamente in aree già compromesse, degradate o interessate da attività industriali dismesse, senza consumare e impermeabilizzare nuovo suolo", ha affermato la senatrice del Movimento 5 Stelle Elena Sironi.

item.title: One Indian killed in attack on ship heading towards India, Indian embassy in Oman says
item.description: One Indian national was killed in an attack on the bulk carrier MV Cape Dao while the vessel was heading towards India, the Indian embassy in Oman said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: One Indian national was killed in an attack on the bulk carrier MV Cape Dao while the vessel was heading towards India, the Indian embassy in Oman said on Wednesday. The embassy was in close coordination with Omani authorities regarding the safety of all crew on board, including 19 Indian nationals, it added. Oman's Maritime Security Center said on Wednesday that it carried out an evacuation operation for the crew of the vessel following the attack off the sultanate's Musandam governorate. A total of 27 crew members were evacuated, the center said, and one crew member was killed without disclosing his nationality.

item.title: POINT MARCHÉS L'Europe finit dans le rouge, l'obligataire à nouveau sous pression
item.description: Les Bourses européennes ont terminé en baisse mercredi, sous l'effet d'une nouvelle hausse des prix du pétrole et des rendements obligataires, les dernières déclarations des dirigeants américain et iranien jetant le doute quant aux efforts visant à mettre fin au conflit.
item.dc:creator: Diana Mandia
item.content:encoded: Les Bourses européennes ont terminé en baisse mercredi, sous l'effet d'une nouvelle hausse des prix du pétrole et des rendements obligataires, les dernières déclarations des dirigeants américain et iranien jetant le doute quant aux efforts visant à mettre fin au conflit. Une série de données indiquant que l'activité économique résiste tant aux États-Unis qu'en Europe - ce qui va dans le sens d'une politique plus restrictive de la part des banques centrales - a encore accentué cette tendance. À Paris, le CAC 40 (.FCHI) a perdu 0,39% à 8.123,41 points. À Francfort, le Dax (.GDAXI) a reculé de 0,59% et à Londres, le FTSE 100 (.FTSE) a abandonné 0,03%. L'indice EuroStoxx 50 (.STOXX50E) a fini sur un recul de 0,31%, le FTSEurofirst 300 (.FTEU3) a perdu 0,39% et le Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) a reculé de 0,37%. Les cours du pétrole ont mis fin à une série de cinq séances de baisse et le Brent est repassé au-dessus des 100 dollars le baril, ce qui remet au premier plan les pressions inflationnistes qui devraient conduire les banques centrales à resserrer encore davantage leur politique monétaire. Le Brent , qui avait atteint mardi son plus bas niveau en deux semaines, à 97,36 dollars le baril, progresse de 3,52% mercredi pour s'établir à 102,74 dollars, tandis que le brut léger américain (West Texas Intermediate, WTI) gagne 2,28% à 92,58 dollars. Les Etats-Unis et l'Iran ont repris contact mardi à New York, leurs premières discussions indirectes depuis l'effondrement d'un cessez-le-feu en juillet dernier, mais chaque partie campe pour l'heure sur ses positions. Le président iranien, Massoud Pezeshkian, [USN:L8N45F1A8 TEXT:"a exclu"] toute capitulation dans un discours prononcé mercredi devant l'Assemblée générale des Nations unies au lendemain d'une nouvelle menace de Donald Trump, qui a averti devant le même auditoire qu'il pourrait "annihiler" l'Iran si aucun accord de paix n'était conclu. Les données économiques plus solides que prévu dans ce contexte d'inflation laissent penser que les banques centrales auront les mains libres pour resserrer leurs taux d'intérêt sans craindre de nuire à l'activité. L'indice PMI composite de la production aux États-Unis, qui reflète l'évolution des secteurs industriel et des services, a atteint en septembre son plus haut niveau depuis plus de cinq ans, ce qui a rapidement renforcé les anticipations d'une hausse des taux d'intérêt par la Réserve fédérale (Fed) en octobre. Les opérateurs tablent désormais sur une probabilité de 73% d'une hausse des taux en octobre, contre 53% auparavant. Ces anticipations se sont une nouvelle fois répercutées sur le marché obligataire, où les rendements des bons du Trésor américain à 10 ans ont de nouveau dépassé les 5% et atteint leur plus haut niveau depuis 2007. Dans la zone euro, l'activité du secteur privé [USN:ZRN00EKPS TEXT:"a accéléré"] en septembre à son rythme le plus rapide depuis plus de trois ans, tandis que les coûts d'exploitation des entreprises ont encore augmenté. Les rendements se sont également tendus mercredi dans la zone euro, accentuant encore davantage la pression sur un marché obligataire qui souffre également des inquiétudes concernant les finances publiques, notamment en France. VALEURS A Paris, TotalEnergies (TTEF.PA) a fini sur un gain de 1,8%, aidé par la hausse des prix du pétrole. Le secteur de l'énergie sur le Stoxx 600 (.SXEP) (+1,34%) a été, avec la défense (.SXPARO) (+1,29%), le seul à enregistrer des gains significatifs mercredi. JD Sports (JD.L) a reculé de 5,7% alors que le distributeur d'articles de sport a fait était d'une baisse de 19,7% de son bénéfice semestriel. Arcadis (ARDS.AS) a abandonné près de 3%, après que la société d'ingénierie canadienne WSP Global WSP.TO a retiré son offre publique d'achat sur la société néerlandaise de conseil et d'ingénierie. A WALL STREET Les anticipations renforcées sur le resserrement de la politique monétaire de la Fed entraînent un recul des indices de la Bourse de New York. A l'heure de la clôture en Europe, le Dow Jones (.DJI) perd 0,52%, le Standard & Poor's 500 (.SPX) 0,55% et le Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) 0,93%. Meta (META.O) prend en revanche 2,7%, poursuivant ainsi ses les gains liés à "Muse", son assistant IA lancé ce mois-ci. TAUX Le marché de la dette souveraine a fortement réagi aux craintes inflationnistes et aux données économiques solides publiées des deux côtés de l'Atlantique. Aux Etats-Unis, le rendement des Treasuries à dix ans s'envole de 10,4 points de base pour s'établir à 5,0706%, tandis que celui de l'obligation à deux ans prend près de 9 points de base à 4,8661%. Dans la zone euro, le rendement du Bund allemand à dix ans a pris 9 points de base à 3,5450%. Le deux ans a gagné 7,8 points de base à 3,2850%. En France, le rendement de l'OAT à dix ans a grimpé de 14,6 points de base pour finir la séance à 4,638%, un plus haut depuis 2008. Le "spread", ou écart de rendement entre l'obligations allemandes et françaises à 10 ans s'est encore amplifié mercredi pour atteindre les 110 points de base (pdb). Il avait dépassé vendredi les 100 pdb pour la première fois depuis 2012. CHANGES Le dollar prend 0,47% face à un panier de devises de référence (.DXY) et évolue à son plus haut niveau depuis près de deux mois, les investisseurs anticipant un cycle de hausse des taux de la Fed. L'euro perd 0,5% à 1,1390 dollar . A SUIVRE LE 24 SEPTEMBRE : [USN:L8N45B02I] (Certaines données peuvent accuser un léger décalage)

item.title: Ronaldo eyes 1,000-goal 'icing on the cake' as Portugal begin new era
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo walked into a packed room, claimed to be nervous, then did what he has done for more than two decades: taking centre stage, swatting away critics and insisting the final whistle is not yet in sight.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Kallas
item.content:encoded: Cristiano Ronaldo walked into a packed room, claimed to be nervous, then did what he has done for more than two decades: taking centre stage, swatting away critics and insisting the final whistle is not yet in sight. The 41-year-old Portugal captain, speaking on Wednesday at the Portugal Football Summit main stage before Thursday's UEFA Nations League match against Wales, said he still had plenty to offer his country as Jorge Jesus prepares for his first game as national team coach. Jesus replaced Roberto Martinez after Portugal's disappointing World Cup campaign ended in the round of 16 against eventual champions Spain. Ronaldo, now on 979 career goals — 833 for clubs and 146 for Portugal — is 21 short of the 1,000-goal landmark he has openly targeted. Asked whether winning the Nations League or reaching four figures mattered more, he grinned and chose both. "One goal is to achieve both – reaching 1,000 goals and the national team trying to win this Nations League," Ronaldo said at the Portugal Football Summit at the Portuguese FA headquarters outside Lisbon. "It's a new era with manager Jorge Jesus, whom we all know well; I just hope things go well for him." Ronaldo said reaching 1,000 in Portugal colours would be "the icing on the cake". "Scoring my 1,000th goal for the national team would be the culmination of something – a beautiful story," he said. "It wouldn't be the end of it, but it would be a beautiful story." Ronaldo insisted, however, that he was not consumed by the chase. "I've already admitted that I want to get there, and I will get there," he said. "An obsession? No ... The rest is about enjoying it, enjoying every day." PRODUCTIVE TALKS Ronaldo acknowledged he had considered his international future after Portugal's World Cup exit, but said talks with the Portuguese FA and Jesus convinced him to continue. "They count on me. I still believe that I'm able to help the national team," he said. "The most important point is to be able, inside the pitch, to score goals and help the team to win games. "If the manager doesn't count on me, I can leave today – no problem at all... When I feel that I'm not doing anything here, that I'm not contributing on the pitch, not scoring goals, creating a bad atmosphere, or that they don't want me here, I'll be the first to pack my bags." Pressed on retirement, Ronaldo refused to draw a clear line under his career. "I learnt something from my late 30s onwards, which is to live in the moment, don't think about tomorrow," he said. "Is it possible? Yes. Highly likely? Yes. But will it happen? No, I don't know." Ronaldo also bristled at criticism, saying media outlets had been trying to "kill" him for years. "That's not going to happen under any circumstances – not even with a shotgun," he said. "And even so, I still manage to dodge the bullet." Ronaldo may be 21 goals from four figures and perhaps closer to the exit than he cares to admit, but for now he remains exactly where he likes to be: in Portugal's shirt, in front of the cameras, and dodging bullets with a smile.

item.title: Ashtead Technology receives $660 million takeover proposal from Ember
item.description: British subsea technology firm Ashtead Technology on Wednesday said it has received a non-binding indicative proposal from Ember Infrastructure Management that values the company at about £498 million ($659.75 million).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British subsea technology firm Ashtead Technology (ATAS.L) on Wednesday said it has received a non-binding indicative proposal from Ember Infrastructure Management that values the company at about £498 million ($659.75 million). Here are some more details: Ashtead said Ember has proposed to acquire the company for 615 pence per share in cash. The offer represents a 12.8% premium to Ashtead's last closing price of 545 pence. The proposal follows three previous approaches from Ember, the first two of which were rejected by the board, Ashtead said. The company is considering the latest proposal with its advisers, it added. Under UK takeover rules, Ember has until October 21 to announce a firm intention to make an offer or say it does not intend to proceed. ($1 = 0.7548 pounds)

item.title: Why new war in Ethiopia’s Tigray threatens to trigger wider conflict
item.description: Regional forces in northern Ethiopia's Tigray on Wednesday seized control of three airports and clashed in multiple locations with federal troops, signalling the start of a major offensive after months of growing tensions.
item.dc:creator: David Lewis
item.content:encoded: Regional forces in northern Ethiopia's Tigray on Wednesday seized control of three airports and clashed in multiple locations with federal troops, signalling the start of a [USN:L6N45F0AV TEXT:"major offensive"] after months of growing tensions. The move shatters a peace deal that ended the 2020-2022 conflict between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and federal forces, and comes amid a backdrop of deteriorating ties between Ethiopia and Eritrea, Sudan's civil war, tensions over Red Sea access, and the Horn of Africa being dragged into Middle East conflicts. WHY DOES NEW FIGHTING IN TIGRAY THREATEN A WIDER WAR IN ETHIOPIA? The Pretoria Agreement, which formally ended a conflict that killed hundreds of thousands of people, has been under strain for months, each side accusing the other of violating the deal. The peace process began to unravel after [USN:L5N3QM0I9 TEXT:"splits"] emerged within the TPLF, and a hardline faction of the party [USN:L6N41I0CO TEXT:"reasserted control"] over the region, kicking out an interim administration. Most recently, the TPLF formed an [USN:L6N45D0K7 TEXT:"alliance"] with six other armed groups from across Ethiopia, including former enemies from the war, aimed at overthrowing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government. It is not clear how many members of the alliance were involved in clashes on Wednesday but Ethiopia is home to many heavily armed regional groups. Abiy's government has accused Eritrea of financially backing members of the alliance, allegations Asmara has denied. WHAT ROLE WILL ERITREA PLAY? As the situation unfolds, all eyes will be on Asmara, which has endured a turbulent relationship with Addis Ababa since independence in 1993. Soon after coming to power, Abiy [USN:KBN1WQ12X TEXT:"won the Nobel Peace Prize"] in 2019 for ending two decades of hostility between Ethiopia and Eritrea. When the civil war erupted the following year, Eritrean forces then supported Ethiopia's federal army. Relations have deteriorated since the Pretoria peace agreement, which Eritrea was not party to despite having fought in the war. Access to the Red Sea is another flash point. Landlocked Ethiopia had a coastline for decades until Eritrea broke away. Since then, Addis Ababa has repeatedly argued that restoring access to the sea - specifically the port of Assab - is vital for its long term security and economic development. Asmara has said it fears Addis Ababa will try to take Assab by force. Earlier this month, the US government [USN:L1N45A0J7 TEXT:"lifted sanctions"] on Eritrean Defense Forces and other entities. It is not clear what impact removing sanctions would have on any conflict in Ethiopia, but the move is seen as a nod by the Trump administration to Eritrea’s [USN:L8N41I1AB TEXT:"strategic coastline"] opposite Saudi Arabia, and warning Ethiopia not to go to war with Asmara. WHICH REGIONAL RISKS RAISE THE STAKES THIS TIME AROUND? Diplomats warn that a renewed Tigray war would no longer be a largely isolated Ethiopian conflict. Instead, it would unfold as the Horn of Africa faces its most volatile security environment in years, with war raging in Sudan, persistent instability in Somalia, tensions over the Nile and expanding war and geopolitics from the Middle East spilling into the region. Ethiopia has been accused of backing the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) paramilitary group, which is fighting Sudan’s army in one of the world’s deadliest conflicts. This support, which Ethiopia denies, is in line with its close relationship with the United Arab Emirates, the most active Gulf power in the region which UN experts say is also supporting the RSF. The UAE has denied the accusations. For its part, Eritrea is closer to Sudan and has cultivated relatively close ties with Egypt, which is a long-time rival of Ethiopia. Egypt and Sudan both see Ethiopia's Grand Ethiopian [USN:L2N3UW04A TEXT:"Renaissance Dam,"] built on a tributary of the Nile, as a serious threat to their vital water supplies.

item.title: Governo abre discussão sobre futuro de concessões hidrelétricas, cita possíveis "travas" em leilões
item.description: O Ministério de Minas e Energia colocou em consulta pública uma proposta de diretrizes sobre o futuro de uma série de concessões de usinas hidrelétricas que vencem até 2032, citando possíveis "travas" em leilões para evitar concentração de mercado entre os grandes grupos hidrelétricos.
item.dc:creator: Leticia Augusto
item.content:encoded: O Ministério de Minas e Energia colocou em consulta pública uma proposta de diretrizes sobre o futuro de uma série de concessões de usinas hidrelétricas que vencem até 2032, citando possíveis "travas" em leilões para evitar concentração de mercado entre os grandes grupos hidrelétricos. A discussão interessa a importantes companhias do setor que possuem portfólios hidrelétricos, como Axia (AXIA3.SA) , Copel (CPLE3.SA) e Engie (EGIE3.SA) . Axia e Copel, que tiveram concessões hidrelétricas renovadas em seus processos de privatização, têm defendido que os próximos ativos vincendos sejam colocados para disputa em leilões, alegando que isso também [USN:S0N43801A TEXT:"maximizaria os ganhos ao governo"]. Já a Engie, com concessões vencendo nos próximos anos, quer a prorrogação de seus contratos. No documento, o ministério não propõe um caminho único -- licitação ou prorrogação -- para os contratos vincendos, que envolvem mais de 15 gigawatts (GW) do parque hidrelétrico brasileiro. Mas, no caso de eventuais leilões, diz que se cogita o estabelecimento de "travas ou limites máximos de aquisição dos ativos no leilão, calibrados pelo 'market share' resultante após os lances". A ideia, segundo a nota técnica, seria evitar que companhias elétricas aumentem seus portfólios hidrelétricos a ponto de serem capazes de exercer influência relevante sobre os preços de energia no país. Essas medidas seriam calibradas para que não reduzam a concorrência nos leilões, e também discutidas com os agentes do setor, órgãos de controle, regulador, operador, planejador, potenciais investidores, bem como os participantes do Sistema Brasileiro de Defesa da Concorrência (SBDC), diz a pasta. Já no caso de prorrogações contratuais, a alternativa ficaria condicionada, por exemplo, à demonstração da prestação do "serviço adequado". Também não haveria antecipação do fim do prazo da outorga atual. Tanto no caso de licitação quanto de prorrogação contratual, as empresas terão que pagar ao governo pelas novas outorgas hidrelétricas. O pagamento pelo valor da outorga ocorrerá 50% à vista, e o restante poderá ser pago em até cinco parcelas anuais, diretamente à Conta de Desenvolvimento Energético (CDE), visando a modicidade tarifária. A previsão é de que as novas outorgas hidrelétricas terão prazo de vinte anos, podendo ainda ter duração inferior. Ao todo, as regras devem alcançar 40 usinas hidrelétricas, que totalizam cerca de 15,4 GW de capacidade instalada, sendo 20 com concessões vencendo até 2029, e outras 20, no horizonte entre 2030 e 2032. Além disso, outras 40 pequenas centrais hidrelétricas (PCHs), com 0,7 GW de capacidade instalada, têm contratos expirando no período.

item.title: Peso mexicano cae a mínimos desde julio por perspectivas de tasas
item.description: El peso mexicano se debilitaba el miércoles a niveles no vistos desde finales de julio, presionado por un avance global del dólar ante expectativas de nuevas alzas de la Reserva Federal, mientras que Banco de México mantendría sin cambios su tasa clave por más tiempo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El peso mexicano se debilitaba el miércoles a niveles no vistos desde finales de julio, presionado por un avance global del dólar ante expectativas de nuevas alzas de la [USN:L1N4580T6 TEXT:"Reserva Federal"], mientras que Banco de México mantendría sin cambios su tasa clave por más tiempo. En el frente geopolítico, la sesión estaba marcada por esperanzas de avances hacia el fin de la guerra en [USN:L6N45F0QQ TEXT:"Medio Oriente"]. Los inversionistas se preparaban además para un encuentro previsto el jueves entre el presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, y su par chino, [USN:L6N45F08F TEXT:"Xi Jinping"]. * La moneda local se negociaba en 17.4836 unidades por dólar, con una depreciación de un 1.2%, a medida que la [USN:L6N45F0IM TEXT:"divisa estadounidense"] alcanzaba su nivel más alto en dos meses y los [USN:L6N45F0J7 TEXT:"precios del petróleo"] reanudaban su tendencia alcista. * Previamente, el peso llegó a superar marginalmente el umbral de 17.50, identificado por analistas como un techo técnico para sus operaciones de corto plazo. Posteriormente, redujo parte de sus pérdidas y volvió a ubicarse por debajo de esa zona, aunque persistía la presión sobre la moneda. * "El nivel de 17.50 pesos por dólar es una resistencia importante", dijo Humberto Calzada, economista jefe de Rankia Latinoamérica. "Hoy el principal soporte proviene de una Reserva Federal restrictiva y de la cautela previa a la decisión de Banco de México", añadió. * Autoridades de la Fed han señalado esta semana que podría ser necesario un mayor endurecimiento monetario si la inflación no cede con suficiente rapidez. El gobernador [USN:L6N45F0SK TEXT:"Michael Barr"] se sumó el miércoles a esos comentarios al decir que probablemente se tendría que aplicar nuevas alzas de tasas de interés. * Ese escenario reduciría el diferencial de tasas con México que durante años ha respaldado las operaciones de "carry trade", una fuente de apoyo para el peso al atraer flujos hacia activos locales. * La atención de los inversores se centraba ahora en la decisión del [USN:L6N45D0SW TEXT:"Banco de México"] el jueves. Si el organismo prolonga la pausa en su tasa de referencia, como espera el mercado, un menor diferencial frente a Estados Unidos podría restar atractivo a la moneda mexicana. * La bolsa, a su vez, caía después de dos jornadas de ganancias, siguiendo el débil desempeño de los mercados en Nueva York. El índice líder S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) bajaba un 0.30%, a 64,263.44 puntos. * Las acciones de la cementera Cemex (CEMEXCPO.MX) encabezaban las pérdidas al caer un 1.41%, a 17.52 pesos. Les seguían los títulos del minero Grupo México (GMEXICOB.MX) , que retrocedían un 1.24%, a 219.51 pesos. * En el mercado secundario de deuda, el rendimiento del bono a 10 años operaba en un 9.35%, sin cambios frente a su cierre previo, mientras que la tasa a 20 años se estabilizaba en un 9.79%.

item.title: Baltic nations seek EU support to combat drones, Lithuania says
item.description: Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia have jointly asked the European Commission for additional financial support from the EU for drone fighting capabilities, Lithuania's Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas said in a statement to Reuters on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia have jointly asked the European Commission for additional financial support from the EU for drone fighting capabilities, Lithuania's Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas said in a statement to Reuters on Wednesday. With Ukraine stepping up long-range drone attacks on Russia, some of the drones have entered airspace in the Baltic region, [USN:L8N41X1AC TEXT:"stoking concerns"] that the war between Moscow and Kyiv is spilling over NATO's borders. Kaunas did not say how much money the countries had asked for. Finnish daily Iltalehti reported that the three Baltic nations had asked for €500 million ($569.45 million). "We are looking into procuring the capabilities jointly, with preference for the European defence industry. This strengthens both our resilience and the industry cooperation in Europe", Kaunas said. ($1 = 0.8780 euros)

item.title: プーチン氏、下院選の高投票率は「軍への支持の表れ」と評価
item.description: [モスクワ ２３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[モスクワ ２３日 ロイター] - ロシアのプーチン大統領は２３日、先週末の下院選挙で高い投票率となったことについて、国民がウクライナで戦うロシア軍や国家安全保障を守る当局の取り組みを支持していることの表れだと述べた。

２１日発表された選挙結果によると、プーチン大統領を支持する与党「統一ロシア」が下院定数４５０議席のうち３５５議席、約８０％を占める見通しとなり、過去最多となる議席を獲得した。

ロシア中央選挙管理委員会によると、投票率は５９．３％だった。国営タス通信は、これは近年の下院選挙の大半を上回る水準だと伝えた。

結果について初めて公にコメントしたプーチン氏は、「これほど多く、さらには記録的ともいえる人数が投票に訪れたことは、ロシア国民が国の強化を目的としたわれわれの取り組みを支持していることを示している」と述べた。

item.title: ULTIM'ORA-UCRAINA: Mosca e Kiev interessate a tregua limitata - Rubio dopo incontro con Lavrov
item.description: Di seguito gli aggiornamenti sul conflitto in corso in Ucraina:
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Di seguito gli aggiornamenti sul conflitto in corso in Ucraina: 17.35 - A seguito dell’incontro tenutosi oggi con il ministro degli Esteri russo Sergei Lavrov, il segretario di Stato Usa Marco Rubio ha detto alla stampa che sia la Russia che l’Ucraina hanno manifestato interesse per un cessate il fuoco limitato che riguardi il grano e l’energia. 14.05 - Un elicottero militare russo Mi-8 ha effettuato una breve incursione nello spazio aereo della Polonia, Paese membro della Nato, partendo dall’exclave russa di Kaliningrad. Lo ha reso noto il Comando operativo dell’esercito polacco. L’elicottero ha trascorso 42 secondi nello spazio aereo polacco, penetrando fino ad una estensione di circa 300 metri, ha scritto il Comando su X. "Sono stati fatti decollare aerei da caccia, mentre le forze e i mezzi di terra sono rimasti in stato di allerta. La natura dell’episodio indica che la Russia sta ancora una volta mettendo alla prova la prontezza della nostra difesa aerea", ha aggiunto 11.35 - Il Cremlino ha affermato oggi che non sussistono ancora i presupposti per l’avvio di colloqui di pace sull’Ucraina, pur rimanendo aperto a tali trattative. Intervenendo in vista di un incontro previsto a New York tra il segretario di Stato Usa Marco Rubio e il ministro degli Esteri russo Sergey Lavrov, ha detto che non vi sono piani concreti per incontri ad alto livello né con Washington né con Kiev al fine di discutere un potenziale accordo di pace. Il portavoce del Cremlino Dmitry Peskov ha affermato che non è cambiata nemmeno la posizione della Russia riguardo alla possibilità di un incontro di persona tra il presidente Vladimir Putin e il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelensky. "Zelensky, se lo desidera, può venire a Mosca. Gli saranno fornite le necessarie garanzie di sicurezza", ha detto Peskov, aggiungendo che il presidente ucraino è consapevole delle decisioni che deve prendere, secondo Mosca. Le autorità ucraine hanno ripetutamente affermato che un incontro a Mosca non sarebbe accettabile e hanno proposto invece di tenere colloqui diretti in un paese neutrale.

item.title: Pezeshkian dice che Iran non si arrenderà, dopo minaccia Trump
item.description: Di seguito gli aggiornamenti sulla situazione in Medio Oriente:
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Di seguito gli aggiornamenti sulla situazione in Medio Oriente: 17.10 - In un discorso alle Nazioni Unite, il presidente iraniano Masoud Pezeshkian ha detto che Teheran non si arrenderà mai agli Stati Uniti, ma continua a credere nella diplomazia, all’indomani delle minacce del presidente Donald Trump, che dallo stesso forum ha minacciato di "annientare" l’Iran. I discorsi presso l’Assemblea Generale annuale dell'Onu a New York hanno fatto da cornice ai primi colloqui indiretti tra Usa e Iran da diversi mesi a questa parte, che sembrano non aver portato ad alcun passo avanti riguardo alla fine della guerra in Medio Oriente. Nel suo discorso, Pezeshkian ha difeso le azioni militari dell’Iran definendole difensive e ha ribadito che il Paese non sta cercando di dotarsi di armi nucleari. L’Iran ha inoltre minacciato di agire contro i propri vicini qualora questi si attenessero alle nuove sanzioni Usa volte a impedire il volo degli aerei civili iraniani in tutto il mondo. 11.30 - Il Board of Peace del presidente Usa Donald Trump presenterà un piano di sei mesi per la ricostruzione di Gaza dal valore di 2,45 miliardi di dollari durante una riunione prevista per oggi. Lo ha riportato Axios. Il piano prevede spese per la costruzione di alloggi temporanei, lo sgombero delle macerie, i lavori di riparazione degli ospedali, la ripresa economica e il dispiegamento di una forza di sicurezza multinazionale, aggiunge l’articolo, citando una copia del piano. Reuters non ha potuto verificare al momento la notizia. 9.10 - L’Iran ha avviato un dialogo con gli Stati Uniti tramite un mediatore del Qatar a New York e ha comunicato alcune condizioni, tra cui la fine del conflitto su tutti i fronti e di quelli che Teheran ha definito “atti di aggressione” da parte degli Stati Uniti. Lo ha riferito il portavoce del ministero degli Esteri iraniano Esmail Baghaei all’agenzia di stampa statale Irna. Baghaei ha detto che tra le condizioni dell’Iran vi è anche la cessazione del blocco navale e della guerra economica, così come lo sblocco dei beni iraniani, secondo quanto riportato da Irna.

item.title: US senators aim to fast-track Chinese vehicle ban this week as Xi visits
item.description: Supporters of legislation to make permanent a ban on Chinese vehicles are aiming to win fast-track approval by the U.S. Senate this week as President Donald Trump meets with China's President Xi Jinping.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Supporters of legislation to make permanent a ban on Chinese vehicles are aiming to win fast-track approval by the U.S. Senate this week as President Donald Trump meets with China's President Xi Jinping. Republican Senator Bernie Moreno, one of the two main authors of the proposed legislative ban, intends to ask for unanimous consent to approve the bill, according to a notice sent to Democratic senators on Wednesday. Last week, automakers and other industry groups urged Trump "to maintain policies that keep the door firmly shut to Chinese automakers seeking to sell, import or manufacture vehicles inside the U.S."

item.title: In calo, greggio sale, rendimenti in rialzo in vista di vertice Usa-Cina
item.description: La Borsa Usa arretra, mentre i prezzi del greggio e i rendimenti dei titoli di Stato salgono, con gli investitori che attendono una svolta nei negoziati per porre fine al conflitto in Medio Oriente, alla vigilia del vertice tra Stati Uniti e Cina.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Borsa Usa arretra, mentre i prezzi del greggio e i rendimenti dei titoli di Stato salgono, con gli investitori che attendono una svolta nei negoziati per porre fine al conflitto in Medio Oriente, alla vigilia del vertice tra Stati Uniti e Cina. ** I prezzi del Brent salgono di oltre il 2% dopo cinque sedute consecutive di ribassi, pur rimanendo vicini al minimo delle ultime due settimane. ** I rendimenti del Treasury a due e dieci anni registrano un leggero aumento, alimentando i timori del mercato sul protrarsi di un elevato costo del denaro. ** Le società legate al settore dei chip sono sotto pressione nelle prime ore di contrattazioni, comprese AMD (AMD.O) , NVIDIA (NVDA.O) e INTEL (INTC.O) . L’indice più ampio dei chip di Philadelphia (.SOX) perde il 2,3%. ** META PLATFORMS (META.O) sale dell’1,1%, consolidando il balzo di oltre il 10% registrato finora questa settimana grazie all’ottima accoglienza riservata all'assistente AI Muse, che secondo gli analisti potrebbe avvantaggiare i titoli delle infrastrutture tecnologiche, alimentando al contempo le discussioni sull'impatto dirompente dell’intelligenza artificiale in alcuni segmenti del mercato. ** I principali istituti di credito, tra cui JPMORGAN CHASE (JPM.N) e GOLDMAN SACHS (GS.N) , si stabilizzano dopo le forti perdite di ieri. Il settore finanziario dell’S&P 500 (.SPSY) è poco mosso dopo aver registrato ieri il calo giornaliero più consistente da marzo. ** Intorno alle 16.40 l’indice Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) perde lo 0,19% a 51.766,90, l’S&P 500 (.SPX) perde lo 0,57% a 7.72,45 e il Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) perde l'1% a 26.968,33.

item.title: CVC buys minority stake in internet infrastructure provider CDN77
item.description: Private equity group CVC has agreed to buy a minority stake in Prague-based internet infrastructure provider CDN77 in a deal that brings in external investment for the first time, the companies said in a statement on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Amy-Jo Crowley, Muvija M
item.content:encoded: Private equity group CVC (CVC.AS) has agreed to buy a minority stake in Prague-based internet infrastructure provider CDN77 in a deal that brings in external investment for the first time, the companies said in a statement on Wednesday. The deal values CDN77 at around $1.9 billion, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters. The statement did not disclose the exact size of the stake nor the financial terms of the transaction. CVC said it was the largest private equity deal in central and eastern Europe's technology sector this year. CDN77 Chief Executive Officer Zdenek Cendra, who founded the business in 2011, will retain a majority stake in the company and continue to lead it, with the majority of its senior team also expected to remain in their roles, the statement said. "What we gain in partnering up with CVC is a sparring partner who has helped companies like ours go from big to much bigger, and who opens doors we could not open ourselves," Cendra said in the statement. CDN77 provides computing power and storage for streaming, gaming and software companies, and can support their AI and store their data. It counts video-on-demand platform Rakuten TV, "Peaky Blinders" producer Banijay, online education group Udemy and streaming platform Starz among its clients. The firm is targeting revenue of about $270 million this year, up from $218 million in 2025, the source said. In the statement, CDN77 said it picked CVC because of its understanding of internet infrastructure and its track record of backing founder-led companies, with its top priority being that customers would "see no difference" the day after the transaction. CVC Senior Managing Director Jakub Canda added that its main task was to allow CDN77 to continue to focus on its customers while at the same time "build faster and go further" wherever they can.

item.title: ONU está optando por “olhar para o outro lado” em disputa pelas Malvinas, diz Milei
item.description: As Nações Unidas optaram por “olhar para o outro lado” na disputa da Argentina com o Reino Unido sobre as Ilhas Malvinas, disse o presidente argentino, Javier Milei, nesta quarta-feira perante os líderes mundiais na Assembleia Geral da ONU.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: As Nações Unidas optaram por “olhar para o outro lado” na disputa da Argentina com o Reino Unido sobre as Ilhas Malvinas, disse o presidente argentino, Javier Milei, nesta quarta-feira perante os líderes mundiais na Assembleia Geral da ONU. Milei criticou duramente a organização internacional por não ter tomado mais medidas em relação à questão. As ilhas, situadas na costa da Argentina, são um território ultramarino britânico com ampla autonomia, cuja soberania a Argentina contesta há muito tempo. (Reportagem de Leila Miller)

item.title: Ludoil to invest €1.3 billion in Sicilian oil refiner after acquisition
item.description: Italy's Ludoil plans to invest €1.3 billion ($1.5 billion) in Sicilian oil refiner ISAB over the next five years, the family-owned energy company said on Wednesday after announcing it had completed the acquisition of 51% of the refiner.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Landini
item.content:encoded: Italy's Ludoil plans to invest €1.3 billion ($1.5 billion) in Sicilian oil refiner ISAB over the next five years, the family-owned energy company said on Wednesday after announcing it had completed the [USN:L8N41Q1HU TEXT:"acquisition"] of 51% of the refiner. The purchase from Cypriot private equity firm GOI Energy will bring ISAB back into Italian hands at a time when the Iran war has disrupted refined product imports from the Middle East, sending prices for [USN:L6N4580TA TEXT:"diesel"] and jet fuel to record highs. ISAB accounts for more than 20% of Italy's refining capacity and the government had to clear Ludoil's acquisition under its so-called golden power regime. "At a time of heightened international tensions the government safeguarded the country's main refining hub... ensuring its strategic importance through targeted measures and supporting its return to Italian ownership," Ludoil said in a statement. Merging ISAB with Ludoil will create an energy group with a turnover of €13 billion, it said. NEW BUSINESS PLAN Ludoil, founded in 1954 by the grandfather of its current chairman and CEO Donato Ammaturo, said it would now start leading the management of the refiner's three sites in Sicily. The new owner will invest to restart and modernize several mothballed ISAB processing units. It will also fund the production of sustainable aviation fuel and hydrogenated vegetable oil at the refiner. The refiner is linked to an exclusive long-term contract with global commodity trader Trafigura until 2033. The supply and offtake agreement commits ISAB to sell approximately 90% of its refined petroleum products to Trafigura while Trafigura supplies ISAB with crude oil and the other raw materials required for refining. Under the deal with GOI Energy, the refiner was valued at €1 billion including debt. The financing, backed by a guarantee from Italian export credit agency SACE, was provided by BPER (EMII.MI) , UniCredit (CRDI.MI) and Monte dei Paschi (BMPS.MI) . GOI Energy was advised on the transaction by law firm BonelliErede. ($1 = 0.8778 euros)

item.title: Race to evacuate war-damaged Gaza buildings after deadly apartment block collapse
item.description: Officials in Gaza say plans to evacuate people from war-damaged buildings after the deadly collapse of an apartment block last week face major challenges, including a lack of demolition equipment and limited land to relocate residents.
item.dc:creator: Nidal Al-Mughrabi, Mahmoud Issa, Dawoud Abu Alkas
item.content:encoded: Officials in Gaza say plans to evacuate people from war-damaged buildings after the deadly collapse of an apartment block last week face major challenges, including a lack of demolition equipment and limited land to relocate residents. Nearly a year since a ceasefire ended major fighting between Israel and Hamas , officials say tens of thousands of people, with few options for shelter, are living in buildings damaged during Israel's military campaign, despite repeated warnings that they should leave. In the early hours of September 16, the danger became clear when the Al-Saada building in Gaza City's Al-Rimal neighbourhood [USN:L1N458094 TEXT:"collapsed"], killing 21 people. At least 45 survivors were rescued from the rubble. Gaza officials say more than 2,000 buildings have been classified as being at risk. Other war-damaged buildings have [USN:L1N3XL0KA TEXT:"previously collapsed"], causing casualties, including amid winter storms. "These buildings now represent ticking time bombs for residents and displaced people in many places," said Husni Muhanna, spokesperson for the Gaza City municipality, adding that this presented a "real danger" with the weather set to deteriorate into the winter. On Sunday, Gaza authorities announced an emergency plan to evacuate people from 255 buildings most at risk of collapse and demolish them. An Egyptian-led relief body had offered to provide transport to move those evacuated to designated shelters, said Ismail Al-Thawabta, head of the Hamas-run Gaza government's media office. But he said the plan faced major obstacles, "including some families refusing to evacuate unsafe buildings despite the warnings, severe funding shortages, a lack of heavy equipment needed for safe demolition, and limited safe land available to relocate displaced people." SHORTAGE OF EQUIPMENT Large-scale reconstruction in Gaza has yet to begin, with [USN:L1N4470Q0 TEXT:"US-brokered efforts"] to get Hamas to disarm and Israeli forces to withdraw largely stalled. A population of more than 2 million lives confined to about a third of the enclave, mainly housed in makeshift tents or overcrowded rooms in damaged buildings. Deadly [USN:L1N45F08X TEXT:"Israeli airstrikes"], which Israel says target militants, have continued. Most of Gaza's buildings were destroyed by airstrikes or bulldozed by Israeli forces, and almost all others have suffered damage. Palestinian and UN officials blame Israel's restrictions on Gaza for the lack of heavy machinery to clear rubble and materials and equipment to rebuild homes. In response to a request for comment, Israel's military said it was committed to minimising harm to civilians and that any activities, including against "terrorist infrastructure", were carried out based on operational necessity. COGAT, the Israeli military agency that coordinates aid, said entry of heavy equipment and reconstruction materials would not be authorised until Hamas disarmed. It said Hamas exploited humanitarian aid, something the Palestinian militant group denies. Alessandro Mrakic, head of the United Nations Development Programme office in Gaza, said a shortage of equipment meant people had to dig through the rubble with their hands when the Al-Saada building collapsed, and that oil and spare parts were needed to keep the machinery already in Gaza in service. He estimated the number of buildings at risk of collapse at 400. "We know that these buildings will collapse, especially now with the upcoming winter," he said. "We are running against time." RESIDENTS SAY THEY HAVE NOWHERE ELSE TO GO The Al-Saada building was in an area that was hit by Israeli bombardment two days after a Hamas-led attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, triggered Israel's offensive in Gaza. Israel launched heavy airstrikes followed by a ground campaign which it said were aimed at destroying Hamas and its underground network of tunnels . Mohammad Arafa, head of the Gaza Engineers Association, said that based on assessments by fellow engineers who inspected the Al-Saada building over the past year, its collapse resulted from structural weakness after bombardment damaged several concrete pillars supporting its foundations. But people had sheltered there because they had nowhere else to go, said Feryal Abu Ghanem, whose daughter-in-law was staying with her family when the building collapsed and was among those killed. Bassam Naseer, a displaced man living in another damaged building nearby, said he feared the same thing would happen there. "No one is looking after us. The conditions are very difficult," he said. After the Al-Saada's collapse, the Israel Defense Forces said in a social media post that it had not struck the building during the war. It did not respond to questions about residents saying it had struck the building, or about whether the building had been damaged by strikes on the surrounding area. Eyad Azzam, who lost his pregnant wife and a 3-year-old son in the Al-Saada building's collapse, showed a video on his mobile phone of another son, Abdel-Rahman, trapped in the wreckage of the building before he was pulled to safety. Abdel-Rahman, 7, had reached towards his mother, hoping to protect her from fallen rock, his father said. "He put out his hand and it wasn't a rock that had fallen, it was the entire ceiling." People continued to live under damaged ceilings or columns for lack of other options, Azzam said. "Today people say, 'This is a dangerous place to live in.' But where shall I go?" he said. "Even in the street there's no place."

item.title: 南ア中銀、政策金利7.25％に引き上げ インフレ率3％への抑制目指す
item.description:
Kopano Gumbi Sfundo Parakozov
[プレトリア ２３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Kopano Gumbi　Sfundo Parakozov

[プレトリア　２３日　ロイター] - 南アフリカ準備銀行（ＳＡＲＢ、中央銀行）は２３日の金融政策委員会（ＭＰＣ）で、政策金利のレポ金利を２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）引き上げ、７．２５％にすることを全会一致で決定した。インフレ率を中銀目標である３％に抑えることを目指していると述べた。

南ア中銀は、インフレ目標３％の上下１％ポイントを許容範囲としている。８月の南ア消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）は前年同月４．４％上昇と、７月の４．３％から伸びが加速した。

ロイターがまとめた調査でエコノミストの大半が２５ｂｐの利上げを予想していた。７月に開かれた前回の会合以降、イラン情勢の緊迫化に伴い原油価格が再び上昇し、世界経済の見通しも悪化している。

item.title: EEUU abierto a extender tregua comercial con China, o tener un mayor acuerdo, dice Bessent
item.description: Estados Unidos está abierto a prorrogar la tregua comercial con China que vence el 10 de noviembre o a considerar un acuerdo comercial posiblemente más amplio, dijo el miércoles el secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, al salir de una reunión con el viceprimer ministro chino, He Lifeng, destinada a preparar la cumbre entre los líderes de ambos países.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal
item.content:encoded: Estados Unidos está abierto a prorrogar la tregua comercial con China que vence el 10 de noviembre o a considerar un acuerdo comercial posiblemente más amplio, dijo el miércoles el secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, al salir de una reunión con el viceprimer ministro chino, He Lifeng, destinada a preparar la cumbre entre los líderes de ambos países. Bessent no ofreció detalles sobre un posible acuerdo comercial de mayor envergadura entre ambas potencias tras su segunda reunión con He en cuatro días. Se prevé que el presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, y el mandatario chino, Xi Jinping, aborden estas cuestiones más a fondo el jueves en la Casa Blanca. "La parte china planteó el domingo la idea de un acuerdo más amplio y, dado que este podría ser un año histórico en el que los líderes se reúnan hasta en cuatro ocasiones... estamos abiertos a la idea de simplemente continuar con el acuerdo de Busan o de examinar la opción de un acuerdo mayor", dijo Bessent a los periodistas. "Nos parecen bien ambas opciones y haremos lo que sea mejor para el pueblo estadounidense", agregó. Previamente, Bessent había descrito la reunión en la sede del Banco Mundial en Washington como una forma de resolver algunos "asuntos pendientes" antes de la cumbre Trump-Xi, y afirmó que la administración Trump buscaba una estabilidad estratégica basada en la "reciprocidad y la equidad". Sin embargo, sus comentarios tras la reunión constituyeron la señal más clara hasta la fecha de que la prórroga de la tregua comercial alcanzada el año pasado en Busan, Corea del Sur, figuraba en la agenda de la cumbre Trump-Xi. Bessent, He y el representante comercial de Estados Unidos, Jamieson Greer, se reunieron el domingo en Nueva York con el objetivo de preparar posibles acuerdos comerciales y sobre inteligencia artificial para que los dos líderes los examinen. Bessent calificó el encuentro como "exitoso" y dijo que ambas partes acordaron poner en marcha una "línea directa" de comunicación para notificarse mutuamente los incidentes relacionados con la seguridad de la IA. La respuesta china no quedó clara y la agencia estatal de noticias Xinhua se limitó a reconocer que ambas partes habían debatido sobre la IA.

item.title: OpenAI says SEC disclosures undermine xAI’s antitrust lawsuit
item.description: ChatGPT maker OpenAI asked a Texas federal judge to throw out an antitrust lawsuit brought by Elon Musk's AI startup xAI before trial, arguing that disclosures by xAI parent company SpaceX SPCX.O undermine claims that Apple's partnership with OpenAI shut out rivals.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: ChatGPT maker OpenAI asked a Texas federal judge to throw out an antitrust lawsuit brought by Elon Musk's AI startup xAI before trial, arguing that disclosures by xAI parent company SpaceX < SPCX.O > undermine claims that Apple's partnership with OpenAI shut out rivals. Here are the details: OpenAI on Tuesday asked US District Judge Mark Pittman in Fort Worth to rule for OpenAI based on the facts so far in the case, which is now set for a trial in January. Musk’s companies sued Apple and OpenAI last year, alleging [USN:L1N3WP1CW TEXT:"Apple violated antitrust law"] by exclusively integrating ChatGPT into Apple Intelligence features on iPhones and other Apple devices. Apple and OpenAI have denied any wrongdoing. Apple previously said its integration deal with OpenAI was not exclusive. X said last week it has [USN:L6N45A08Q TEXT:"settled with Apple"], but the terms have not been disclosed. OpenAI’s new court filing argued that deposition testimony and other evidence bolstered its defense, including recent securities disclosures from Musk’s SpaceX, which [USN:L4N429158 TEXT:"began publicly trading"] in June. SpaceX’s initial public offering registration statement, OpenAI said, is “replete with disclosures diametrically opposed" to xAI's claims of competitive harm alleged in its lawsuit. The registration “bears no resemblance to the doomsaying in this litigation,” it said. OpenAI denied it wields monopoly power, a necessary element to prove antitrust violations. The company also said that by early last year Apple’s “integration of ChatGPT appeared to be off to a slow start,” which was far from signaling a chatbot monopoly among iPhone users. OpenAI said it “cut its forecast for the number of incremental logged-in weekly active users that it expected to obtain as a direct result of the integration.” By the time Musk sued, OpenAI said, “it was clear that Apple’s integration of ChatGPT was dramatically underperforming.” Apple, OpenAI and xAI did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The case is X Corp and SpaceXAI v OpenAI, US District Court for the Northern District of Texas, No. 4:25-cv-00914-P. For X: Craig Reiser and Bradley Justus of Axinn, and Judd Stone II of Stone Hilton For OpenAI: Stephen DiPrima of Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz and Ralph Duggins of Cantey Hanger Read more: [USN:L6N45E05K TEXT:"US opposes part of Apple contempt finding in Epic Games case at US Supreme Court"] [USN:L6N45A08Q TEXT:"US judge denies OpenAI bid to review X Corp’s settlement with Apple"] [USN:L6N43A08F TEXT:"Google defeats consumer lawsuit over Gemini data tracking claims"] [USN:L6N41V17H TEXT:"Musk's failed court attack on OpenAI could leave lasting scars on Altman's reputation"]

item.title: Presidente paraguayo aboga por regreso de Venezuela al Mercosur; reafirma apoyo a Taiwán
item.description: El presidente paraguayo, Santiago Peña, abogó el miércoles por el retorno de Venezuela al bloque sudamericano Mercosur y reafirmó el apoyo de su país a Taiwán, al dirigirse a los líderes mundiales en la Asamblea General de la ONU.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente paraguayo, Santiago Peña, abogó el miércoles por el retorno de Venezuela al bloque sudamericano Mercosur y reafirmó el apoyo de su país a Taiwán, al dirigirse a los líderes mundiales en la Asamblea General de la ONU. Venezuela se incorporó al Mercosur como miembro pleno en 2012, pero fue suspendida de manera definitiva cinco años después cuando sus socios Brasil, Argentina, Paraguay y Uruguay aplicaron el llamado Protocolo de Ushuaia al considerar que hubo una ruptura del orden democrático en el país. Peña, quien visitó Caracas antes de viajar a Nueva York, dijo en su discurso ante la asamblea que su país abrió un canal de diálogo con las autoridades venezolanas y está trabajando en "acciones" para una transición democrática "real y verdadera". "No fui a Venezuela a validar un régimen, no fui a validar absolutamente nada, más bien todo lo contrario. Paraguay ama la democracia y cree que el pueblo venezolano merece también la democracia", dijo el mandatario. "No podemos esperar que los Estados Unidos o alguna potencia del norte resuelvan nuestros problemas (...) queremos una transición con instituciones, con seguridad, con economía, y en nuestro caso integrada al Mercosur", agregó. Está previsto que el presidente de Chile, José Antonio Kast, cuyo país es miembro asociado del bloque, se reúna con la presidenta interina de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, al margen de la Asamblea General el jueves. Una fuente cercana al presidente brasileño, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, dijo por su parte que si bien Brasil está abierto a una reintegración gradual de Venezuela en el Mercosur, cualquier esfuerzo para lograr el retorno de Caracas probablemente tendría que ser liderado por Paraguay. La fuente señaló que el regreso de Venezuela enfrentaría obstáculos importantes, ya que el país debería cumplir con los requisitos del Mercosur, incluidos el Arancel Externo Común y los acuerdos de trato preferencial que rigen el comercio entre los Estados miembros. APOYO A TAIWÁN El mandatario paraguayo apoyó también el reconocimiento de su aliado Taiwán en el sistema de Naciones Unidas y consideró su exclusión como "una mancha" para la organización. Paraguay es el último aliado diplomático que le queda a Taiwán en Sudamérica y uno de los cada vez menos países del mundo que mantienen vínculos formales con la isla que China reclama como propia. "El Paraguay está, y lo digo alto y claro, con Taiwán (...) excluirlo no fortalece al sistema, lo priva de capacidades que puedan beneficiar a todos y es una mancha para estas Naciones Unidas", aseguró. Paraguay y Taiwan son aliados diplomáticos desde hace casi 70 años y todos los presidentes del país sudamericano han dado un fuerte respaldo a la participación de la isla en el sistema de Naciones Unidas en sus discursos ante la asamblea general la última década.

item.title: Trump, Venezuela's Rodriguez discuss debt restructuring, Rubio says
item.description: US President Donald Trump and Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez discussed the restructuring of the South American nation's billions of dollars in sovereign debt, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Simon Lewis, Daphne Psaledakis
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump and Venezuela's interim [USN:L6N3Y508S TEXT:"President Delcy Rodriguez"] discussed the restructuring of the South American nation's [USN:L8N41R217 TEXT:"billions of dollars in sovereign debt, "]US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday. The brief meeting at a reception Trump hosted late on Tuesday on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly came during Rodriguez's [USN:L6N45E138 TEXT:"first trip to the US"] since American forces captured then-President Nicolas Maduro in a January raid. The talks marked a further step in the rapid improvement in US-Venezuela relations since Maduro's removal, with Washington backing efforts to reconnect the South American nation to international lenders and support an economic recovery after years of default, sanctions and isolation. "There's a lot that needs to be fixed in order for Venezuela to be successful," Rubio told reporters. "Debt restructuring is key to that." Rubio said Venezuela had "probably the world's largest sovereign debt that has to be restructured" and said Washington wanted to help, but that "it has to be done in the right way." Venezuela announced in May it would begin restructuring its external debt , which has been in default since 2017. The sovereign and state oil firm Petroleos de Venezuela together have about $60 billion in defaulted bonds outstanding. Analysts estimate total liabilities, including arbitration awards and accrued interest, could reach between $150 billion to $200 billion. Venezuela has not published comprehensive debt statistics in years, and US sanctions imposed in 2017 largely cut it off from Western financial markets. Rubio described the meeting between Trump and Rodriguez as short but important. Rodriguez arrived in New York on Monday with a delegation that has been [USN:L1N45D0KY TEXT:"holding talks"] on energy, mining and debt with US officials, multilateral lenders and companies, sources said. The head of the Inter-American Development Bank has been working to secure approval for a $2.5 billion loan for Venezuela, Reuters reported on Tuesday, but has faced pushback from some members of the lender's board. That loan, while dwarfed by Venezuela's substantial overall debt, would mark a milestone in efforts to restart lending to the country.

item.title: US will either reform IEA on climate issues or leave the group, energy secretary says
item.description: The US might consider leaving the International Energy Agency if there is no alignment on climate issues, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US might consider leaving the International Energy Agency if there is no alignment on climate issues, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on Wednesday. "We're either going to reform the IEA or we will leave the IEA. My strong preference is that we reform it," Wright said at an event in New York hosted by the Wall Street Journal. The Paris-based IEA has provided research and data to industrialized governments for more than half a century to help guide policy around energy security, supply and investment. The United States provides around a quarter of the group's funding. In recent years, the organization had broadened its focus beyond oil and gas supply to include clean energy, as member governments sought input on meeting their goals under the Paris climate agreement and transition away from fossil fuel reliance. But the Trump administration and the oil industry have criticized the IEA's attention on climate change and have been calling on the agency to focus primarily on oil, gas and coal. Wright said he wants to reform the agency to "focus on its core mission - and deliver it well and thoughtfully - not scenarios that are more politically popular."

FAST

Sept 22 - A rise in Japanese bond yields is creating a "reverse carry" opportunity for overseas investors as Bank of Japan interest-rate hikes make the traditional yen-funded carry trade less compelling, Rong Ren Goh, fixed income portfolio manager at Eastspring Investments, said on Wednesday. Japanese asset prices have swung sharply since the US Federal Reserve and BOJ raised rates within two days of each other last week, with a decades-long era of ultra-cheap yen funding potentially giving way to a new dynamic where Japan's own bonds become the more attractive trade. Buying ultra-long Japanese government bonds and hedging yen exposure back into dollars or another developed-market currency could potentially give investors higher yields versus comparable bonds in their home markets, Goh told the Reuters Global Markets Forum. "The 30-year Japanese government bond above 4 per cent, when swapped in any developed-market currency in the world, including the dollar, gives you an FX-hedged yield 100 to 200 basis points higher than the base currency equivalent," he said.

Goh said the traditional yen-funded carry trade - in which investors borrow cheaply in the Japanese currency to buy higher-yielding foreign assets - is no longer a "no-brainer", as markets expect Japan's policy rate to eventually reach around 2 per cent from 1.25 per cent currently. He expects the reverse carry trade to gain broader appeal as investors become more confident of a stabilisation in Japanese bond prices following a selloff that started in 2022. Positioning data showed the net yen long position in the week to September 15 jumped to its highest since July 2025. A sharp move lower for the yen after Friday's 25-bp BOJ rate hike that came with two dissents, which investors interpreted as a dovish tilt at the Japanese central bank, was contained by a report that authorities conducted rate checks in the currency market. The yen is currently up 1.2 per cent versus the dollar month-to-date. Pointing to Japan's steepening yield curve - where the gap between 2- and 30-year JGB yields is more than 200 bps compared with an average of around 80 bps in other core developed markets where curves are flattening - Goh said buying dollar bonds no longer offered "any compelling carry play", even if the differential between U.S. and Japanese interest rates remained wide. Goh said Eastspring - which manages $291 billion in assets - is adding shorter-dated dollar-denominated bonds, while favouring the ultra-long end of the Japanese curve where the firm is gradually building exposure through high-quality corporate and Samurai bonds as it seeks "additional credit spread over and above JGBs to enhance carry further". Samurai bonds are yen-denominated debt issued by foreign governments or companies. Eastspring began 2026 with a relatively "underweight" position on the yen due to uncertainty over Japan's fiscal and monetary policies, but moved to a more neutral stance around August as currency intervention risk became more meaningful, Goh said. item.title: イラン、外交再開へ米に条件提示 ホルムズ海峡航路や制裁停止など
item.description: [国連／ドバイ ２３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[国連／ドバイ ２３日 ロイター] - イラン外務省の報道官は２３日、米国に対し外交再開の条件を伝えたと明らかにした。

報道官によると、イランは２２日、国連総会の合間に仲介役のカタールを通じ、２時間にわたり米国とメッセージを交換し、条件を提示した。条件には、ホルムズ海峡の沿岸国であるイランとオマーンが合意した同海峡の安全航路の受け入れ、経済「テロ」や海上封鎖を含む米国による対イラン措置の停止、凍結資産の解除、あらゆる戦線での戦闘終結が含まれるという。

これに先立ち、イラン高官は、敵対行為の終結に向けたイランの提案に対する米国の対応を精査していると明らかにした。また、両国の立場には依然多くの隔たりがあるものの、外交交渉は続いていると述べた。同高官によると、２２日の米・イラン間接協議では、ホルムズ海峡の再開や米国による対イラン海上封鎖の解除などが議題となった。

item.title: US open to extending China trade truce, or bigger deal, Bessent says after meeting with He
item.description: The United States is open to extending the US-China trade truce that expires on November 10 or considering a possibly larger trade deal, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday as he left a meeting with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng to prepare for a summit between the two countries' leaders.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal
item.content:encoded: The United States is open to extending the US-China trade truce that expires on November 10 or considering a possibly larger trade deal, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday as he left a meeting with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng to prepare for [USN:L6N45E02J TEXT:"a summit"] between the two countries' leaders. Bessent gave no details about a potentially bigger US-China trade deal following his second meeting with He in four days. US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are expected to discuss the issues further at the White House on Thursday. "The Chinese on Sunday came up with the idea of a bigger deal, and given that this could be a historic year where the leaders meet up to four times -- this being the second meeting, in Shenzhen and then in Miami -- we're open to the idea of just continuing the Busan arrangement or examining the bigger deal," Bessent told reporters. "We're fine with both, and we're going to do what's best for the American people." Bessent earlier described the meeting at World Bank headquarters in Washington as clearing up some "unfinished business" ahead of the Trump-Xi summit, and said the Trump administration wanted strategic stability based on "reciprocity and fairness." But his comments after the meeting were the strongest signal yet that an extension of the trade truce struck last year in Busan, South Korea was on the agenda for the Trump-Xi summit. Bessent, He and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer [USN:L1N45B04Y TEXT:"met in New York on Sunday"] in an effort to tee up potential trade and artificial intelligence agreements for the two leaders to consider. Bessent has characterized those talks as "successful," saying that two sides had agreed to launch a communications "hotline" for notifying each other about AI safety incidents. China's response to the AI hotline plan was unclear, with state news agency Xinhua acknowledging only that the two sides discussed AI. US-China analysts say expectations on AI cooperation are low due to a lack of mutual trust on the technology and because neither side has expressed serious interest in slowing down development. In fact, Trump has said the opposite, that he would not "stifle" AI growth and would maintain the US lead over China in what he now calls "super intelligence." The Bessent-Greer-He meeting on Sunday left unresolved the fate of a nearly year-long trade truce between Washington and Beijing, which expires on November 10. The truce dramatically lowered bilateral tariff rates that had quickly escalated to triple digits and after tit-for-tat retaliation over Trump's tariff hikes last year. China also had agreed to restore the flow of rare earth magnets and other critical minerals that it had severely restricted. Greer told Bloomberg TV on Monday that discussions about extending the trade truce would continue because there was time. "But my expectation is we'll continue talking and I think both sides want it," he said of a trade truce extension. Greer added that the US needed to keep pressure on China to ensure compliance on its critical minerals agreements. US officials last week told reporters that the delivery of rare earths by China "has not been up to par." On Sunday, the two sides discussed other topics that had been previously discussed by Trump and Xi at a May meeting in Beijing, including lowering mutual tariffs on some non-strategic goods and Chinese purchases of Boeing aircraft and agricultural goods. Greer had said the two sides agreed to "operationalize" a process agreed in May for each side to identify potential tariff cuts on non-strategic goods, called the "Board of Trade." He said these could include Chinese exports such as "consumer goods, low-tech items," he said, while US exports for this treatment could include energy, agricultural goods and medical devices, he added.

FAST

NEW YORK, Sept 23 : The US dollar rose to its highest level in nearly two months on Wednesday as investors priced in a rate hike cycle from the Federal Reserve, while oil prices jumped as comments from Iran cast doubt on progress in peace talks. In the wake of the central bank's rate hike last week, comments from several Federal Reserve officials have also flagged the possibility of more rate increases if inflation does not cool. On Wednesday, Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said the US central bank took an important step last week to "recalibrate" short-term borrowing costs to bring down inflation, and will likely need to deliver further interest rate hikes. "It's a rate story right now," said Elias Haddad, global head of markets strategy at Brown Brothers Harriman in London.

"What's driving the dollar higher is a follow through from the hawkish Fed hike that we got last week and that's just given the dollar some renewed momentum. This week there hasn't been much data, or policy relevant data, but what was interesting is the comments from Fed officials, they're basically all toeing the same line that more tightening is in the pipeline." The dollar extended gains after S&P Global said its flash US Composite PMI Output Index, which tracks the manufacturing and services sectors, increased to 58.4 this month, its highest since July 2021, after a 56.0 reading in August, powered by a surge in new orders, though strong demand strained supply chains and pushed prices higher. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, rose 0.54 per cent to 101.09 after hitting 101.1, its highest since July 29. Expectations the Fed will hike rates by at least 25 basis points at its October meeting shot up to about 75 per cent after the data, according to LSEG data, up from roughly 53 per cent before the release. Further fueling gains in the greenback was a rise in oil prices, after Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said in an interview with state TV that as long as Iran's conditions are not met, the Strait of Hormuz would not be reopened and there would be no negotiations. Hopes that diplomacy at the UN General Assembly could lead to a resolution to the seven-month-long Middle East war had helped push oil prices lower since reaching a four-month high in mid-September, but have since reversed course this week. The euro was down 0.52 per cent at $1.1386 and on pace for its third straight daily decline. Earlier S&P Global Flash Euro Zone Composite PMI Output Index data showed the region's economy is showing unexpected signs of health even as conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine drive up energy costs for firms and households. Investors are also waiting for a high-stakes meeting between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping as the two leaders seek stability in a relationship as the superpowers' tensions over trade, technology and Tehran will play out. The dollar strengthened 0.20 per cent to 6.712 versus the offshore Chinese yuan. The Japanese yen weakened 0.6 per cent against the greenback to 158.32 per dollar as traders remain wary of the threat of intervention after the Bank of Japan's rate hike to a 31-year high last week fell short of reassuring investors that more increases may be on the way. Japanese markets are closed for a holiday and this period of lower liquidity makes it a higher probability for authorities to intervene, according to analysts.

Source: Reuters

item.description: [ニューヨーク ２３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ニューヨーク ２３日 ロイター] - ルビオ米国務長官は２３日、トランプ大統領が今年後半に開催されるアジア太平洋経済協力会議（ＡＰＥＣ）首脳会議や２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０）首脳会議に合わせ、中国と再び対話する機会があるとの認識を示した。

item.title: 米国務長官、ロ・ウが限定的停戦に関心 プーチン氏のＧ２０出席に期待
item.description:
[ニューヨーク ２３日 ロイター] - ルビオ米国務長官は２３日、ロシアとウクライナの双方が、穀物とエネルギーに関する限定的な停戦に関心を示しているとの認識を示した。ロシアのラブロフ外相とのニューヨークでの会談後に記者団に語った。
ルビオ長官は記者団に対し、「双方が穀物とエネルギーに関する限定的な停戦に関心を示していると思う。もちろん、それも容易ではないだろう」と述べた。
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ニューヨーク ２３日 ロイター] - ルビオ米国務長官は２３日、ロシアとウクライナの双方が、穀物とエネルギーに関する限定的な停戦に関心を示しているとの認識を示した。ロシアのラブロフ外相とのニューヨークでの会談後に記者団に語った。

ルビオ長官は記者団に対し、「双方が穀物とエネルギーに関する限定的な停戦に関心を示していると思う。もちろん、それも容易ではないだろう」と述べた。 ロシアとウクライナの関心を実現に導くため、米国が建設的な役割を果たすことに前向きだとも述べた。

その上で、両国の戦争において、エネルギーを標的とした攻撃が戦術上の優先課題の中核を成していることが、特に困難な点であると指摘した。

ロシアはウクライナとの海上またはエネルギー分野の停戦に応じる用意があるとの意向を公には示しておらず、ラブロフ氏との会談後にロシア側で何らかの動きがあったことをルビオ氏が示唆したのかどうかはすぐには明らかにならなかった。

ルビオ長官はまた、プーチン大統領が２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０）首脳会議への招待を受け入れることを期待するとし、プーチン氏が出席することになれば、トランプ大統領と会談する機会になるだろうとの認識を示した。

item.title: 米エネ長官、ＩＥＡ離脱の可能性示唆 気候問題で足並み揃わなければ

[ニューヨーク　２３日　ロイター] - ライト米エネルギー長官は２３日、気候問題で足並みが揃わない場合、米国は国際エネルギー機関（ＩＥＡ）からの離脱を検討する可能性があるとの考えを示した。

item.title: Paraguai defende retorno da Venezuela ao Mercosul
item.description: O presidente do Paraguai, Santiago Peña, pediu nesta quarta-feira a reintegração da Venezuela ao bloco comercial sul-americano Mercosul, ao se dirigir aos líderes mundiais na Assembleia Geral da ONU.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente do Paraguai, Santiago Peña, pediu nesta quarta-feira a reintegração da Venezuela ao bloco comercial sul-americano Mercosul, ao se dirigir aos líderes mundiais na Assembleia Geral da ONU. A Venezuela foi suspensa por tempo indeterminado como membro do Mercosul, que reúne algumas das maiores economias da América do Sul, incluindo Brasil, Argentina, Paraguai e Uruguai. O presidente do Chile, José Antonio Kast, cujo país é membro associado do bloco, deve se reunir com a presidente interina da Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, à margem da Assembleia Geral nesta quinta-feira. Em seu discurso, Peña também afirmou que deseja ver a Venezuela passar por uma transição democrática genuína e duradoura. “Queremos uma transição com instituições fortes, segurança, uma economia próspera e uma nação novamente integrada à comunidade internacional e, especificamente, integrada ao Mercosul”, afirmou. Peña visitou Caracas antes de chegar a Nova York, reabrindo o diálogo após o rompimento das relações diplomáticas em 2025 devido às disputadas eleições de 2024 na Venezuela. A Venezuela foi suspensa do Mercosul em 2017 por não cumprir as regras do bloco, e este endureceu sua postura posteriormente, após a detenção de várias figuras da oposição sob o governo do presidente deposto Nicolás Maduro. Embora o Brasil esteja aberto a uma reintegração gradual da Venezuela ao bloco, qualquer esforço para trazer Caracas de volta ao seio do Mercosul provavelmente teria de ser liderado pelo Paraguai, segundo uma fonte próxima ao presidente brasileiro Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. A fonte afirmou que o retorno da Venezuela enfrentaria obstáculos significativos, já que o país precisaria cumprir os requisitos do Mercosul relativos a regras comerciais e tarifárias. APOIO A TAIWAN O Paraguai é o último aliado diplomático de Taiwan na América do Sul e um dos poucos países no mundo que ainda mantêm laços formais com Taipé. Peña aproveitou seu discurso na ONU para reafirmar o apoio do Paraguai em um momento em que Pequim intensificou a pressão militar e política sobre Taiwan, governado democraticamente, que Pequim reivindica como seu próprio território. “Reafirmo aqui hoje meu apoio à participação plena e significativa da República da China (Taiwan) nas Nações Unidas e em suas agências especializadas. Taiwan tem contribuições concretas a oferecer para a paz, o desenvolvimento e os direitos humanos”, disse Peña.

FAST

Sept 23 : OVHcloud CEO Octave Klaba on Tuesday estimated operators of Europe's proposed AI gigafactories would need annual sales of 300 million euros to 400 million euros just to break even on facilities built around fast-depreciating graphics chips.  Klaba said a proposed 200-million-euro public commitment to buy AI services over five years was too small to underpin the scale of private investment required and said focus on national markets prevented OVHcloud from joining existing French consortia.  The EuroHPC program is seeking industry consortia to build and operate up to seven AI gigafactories: large computing facilities for training, fine-tuning and running AI models. "Any national strategy is doomed to failure: there are simply not enough customers to make investments of this size profitable. In our view, national demand is too weak and we must operate on a European scale," he said.
